title: Build mms-toggle + structural a11y test infrastructure redesign, full-component audit, and remediation
notes:
Merged in PR #81. SCOPE EXPANDED 2026-08-06 (J directive, verbatim): "effective immediately, this ticket now is solving for both structural a11y setup, audit, and remediations + toggle component development." Triggered by J catching an overclaim of a11y compliance after a real hover-state WCAG 1.4.11 defect was found and fixed in mms-toggle — J required a systematic, evidence-based audit (not a one-off patch) before any further claims of coverage.

PART 1 — Toggle component build (original scope, DONE, pending-review): Marina markup reused, mms CSS applied. Component + Storybook (Overview + Playground) + 44 unit tests + toggle.a11y.ts built. Fixed a genuine showIcon boolean-attribute defect via a custom Lit ComplexAttributeConverter (defaultTrueBooleanConverter) — showIcon is the only mms property that defaults true, so show-icon="false" as a plain HTML attribute previously had no effect for static-HTML consumers (AEM/Drupal). Removed unused --_on-fill CSS var during self-audit. All 6 /test-component layers pass. Also fixed mid-ticket: mms-toggle hover-halo used --color-surface-hover as a solid fill behind the unchecked track (~1.11:1 light / 1.15:1 dark contrast against surface — fails WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor); changed to a border-ring using --color-border-interactive. Added Hover state + Dark mode describe blocks to toggle.a11y.ts (dark mode forced via Storybook's `&globals=backgrounds.value:dark` query, not manual data-mode).

PART 2 — Structural audit findings (evidence gathered 2026-08-06, via direct source reads + grep across all components, plus a live unfiltered axe scan against the running Storybook instance — not inference):
  - Confirmed IDENTICAL hover-halo contrast defect in mms-checkbox and mms-radio (same --color-surface-hover-as-solid-fill pattern, same component structure). NOT YET FIXED.
  - Zero a11y test files exist for: mms-button, mms-link, mms-checkbox, mms-radio, mms-checkbox-group.
  - No component's a11y suite (select/text-field/text-area/radio-group/modal/toggle) tests hover state or dark mode EXCEPT toggle (fixed this ticket).
  - radio-group has no 'Readonly state' describe block at all, unlike select/text-field/text-area/toggle.
  - select.a11y.ts, text-area.a11y.ts, text-field.a11y.ts, toggle.a11y.ts all use a copy-pasted expectNoA11yViolationsExcludingDisabled helper that suppresses axe's color-contrast rule for READONLY state tests, citing the WCAG 1.4.3 'inactive UI component' exemption — but that exemption applies to DISABLED elements, not readonly ones (readonly remains focusable/operable). Live-verified via unfiltered axe scan that this suppression does NOT currently mask a real defect for toggle's readonly+checked state specifically; select/text-field/text-area are UNVERIFIED.
  - scripts/contrast-audit.mjs implements real WCAG contrast math (gamma-corrected luminance, tier-aware) and passes 296/296 checks, but is never invoked from package.json or .github/workflows/ci.yml — it provides zero actual gate today. It also only validates canonical token-pair combinations (e.g., brand fill vs page background), not runtime-composited combinations like tint-as-hover-fill (the actual defect class found) — so even wiring it in as-is would not have caught this.
  - .claude/skills/test-component/SKILL.md Layer 2 (axe-core) pass criterion is just "0 violations" from `npm run test:a11y` — no requirement for hover-state, dark-mode, or color-scheme coverage. CI's accessibility step is the same bare `npm run test:a11y` call. This is the root-cause process gap that let the same defect ship silently three times.

PART 3 — Remaining work under this ticket's expanded scope:
  (a) Design + implement structural a11y test infrastructure redesign: make hover-state + dark-mode + color-scheme coverage a required, systematically-enforced part of every component's a11y suite (not ad hoc per-file copy-paste); decide contrast-audit.mjs's fate (extend to cover runtime-composited fills + dark mode + wire into CI/test-component, or retire in favor of per-component runtime tests); update test-component/SKILL.md Layer 2 pass criteria and ci.yml accordingly.
  (b) Full audit across all 12 components against the redesigned standard.
  (c) Remediate confirmed defects: checkbox + radio hover-halo (same border-ring fix as toggle) plus net-new hover+dark-mode a11y test files for both. Verify (and fix if needed) the readonly-contrast-exclusion pattern in select/text-field/text-area. Decide on button/link/checkbox-group's total lack of a11y test coverage.
  (d) Flagged, not yet resolved (carried from original scope): the 'toggle/checkbox/radio only, no label' pattern has no aria-label/aria-labelledby passthrough into the shadow-DOM input — test marked test.fixme pending J's call on scope (new ticket vs. fold into this one's remediation pass).

CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (J challenge, verified): the WCAG 1.4.11 framing above for toggle's hover fill was an overclaim — 1.4.11's 3:1 floor applies to information REQUIRED to identify a component/state; hover is a supplementary pointer-only affordance, not required information (checked state, boundary, and focus ring remain independently perceivable without it). The border-ring fix was reverted; toggle's `.hover-bg` is back to a solid-fill pattern matching checkbox/radio. The REAL issue (per J, verified against ui-kit source): mms's flat `--color-surface-hover` (identical `--color-neutral-3` across all 6 themes/colorSchemes) is a design-consistency gap versus Marina, whose equivalent tokens (`--global-fill-brand-hover-control`, `--toggle-oncircle-hover`) are brand/theme-scoped. Fix (J's direction): scope the hover fill per colorScheme using the SAME `--_fill`/`--_fill-hover` custom-property mechanism toggle/checkbox/radio already have, not a new global token. Implemented directly in this ticket for mms-toggle: added `--_hover-bg: var(--color-{scheme}-2)` to each `:host([color-scheme='X'])` block (default/secondary/accent/onyx), changed `.hover-bg`'s hover rule from `background: var(--color-surface-hover)` to `background: var(--_hover-bg)`. Verified live in Storybook (port 6032): `--_hover-bg` resolves to `#F5F1FD` (secondary-2, maximus theme) and the rendered `.hover-bg` background matches on real `:hover` (not synthetic). Step-2 confirmed present for primary/secondary/accent/onyx across all 6 theme files — no fallback needed (unlike `--_fill-hover`'s step-10→9 fallback for Tier 3 palettes lacking step-10). Checkbox and radio need the identical fix but are tracked separately in DS-146 (their own ticket/worktree, per J: toggle must be fixed in DS-032 itself, not deferred). DS-146 was briefly miswritten to include toggle in its scope, then corrected back to checkbox/radio-only once J clarified toggle's fix belongs here.

CENTERING BUG FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-06 (J report): "the hover circle is not exactly center-aligned with the circle that's hovering." Root cause: the checked-state `.hover-bg` left-offset formula (`calc(100% - var(--size-lg2) + 2px)`) was structurally copied from Marina's checked-state hover-layer formula (`width - hoverSize + xs1`), which only self-consistently centers when `hoverSize = thumbSize + 4×xs1` — true for Marina's own dimensions (28px halo = 20px thumb + 4×2px) but false for mms's (32px halo ≠ 20px thumb + 4×2px = 28px). mms uses a larger 32px halo against the same 20px thumb, so the borrowed formula landed 2px off-center (thumb center 36px vs hover-bg center 34px, in the 48px-wide wrapper) — confirmed via direct arithmetic before editing. Fix: derived the checked-state offset the same way the (already-correct) unchecked-state offset was derived — `thumb.left − halfDiff`, where `halfDiff = (haloSize − thumbSize) / 2 = 6px`. New rule: `left: calc(100% - var(--size-md2) - 2px - 6px)` (= `calc(100% - 28px)`), mirroring `:host([checked]) .thumb`'s own `calc(100% - var(--size-md2) - 2px)` minus the 6px halo margin. Verified live in Storybook (port 6032, secondary colorScheme): both checked and unchecked states now show diffX: 0, diffY: 0 between `.hover-bg` and `.thumb` bounding-box centers, confirmed under a real browser_hover (not synthetic) with the hover tint (rgb(245,241,253), secondary-2) rendering correctly. No comparable check has yet been run against checkbox/radio (DS-146, out of scope here) — worth flagging when that ticket is picked up, since their `.hover-bg`/thumb-or-dot geometry may carry the same class of bug if it was derived the same way.

HOVER VISUAL DIRECTION CHANGED 2026-08-06 (J-directed iteration, confirmed): after the centering fix, J asked to preview a 1px `--color-{scheme}-8` border on `.hover-bg` (kept `box-sizing: border-box` so the 32px total size and centering were unaffected), then iterated to a 2px border (`--border-width-sm` instead of `--border-width-xs`), then requested the hover FILL be changed to match the thumb's own color (`--color-surface-raised`) instead of the colorScheme-tint (`--color-{scheme}-2`) approach implemented earlier — producing a "thumb enlarging inside a bordered ring" visual rather than a separate tint appearing behind it. J confirmed this final direction ("I like this much better. let's move forward with this visual direction"). Implemented: removed the now-unused `--_hover-bg` custom property (the `--color-{scheme}-2` tint mechanism from the earlier fix), added `--_hover-border: var(--color-{scheme}-8)` to each `:host([color-scheme='X'])` block (accent keeps a step-8→9 fallback, mirroring `--_fill-hover`'s existing step-10→9 fallback pattern — accent has no step-8 in Tier 3, and is structurally never a valid interactive colorScheme in any theme per `theme-constraints.ts`, so this fallback is defensive/unreachable in the live UI, same as the precedent it mirrors). `.hover-bg` hover rule now sets `background: var(--color-surface-raised)` (matching thumb) and `border-color: var(--_hover-border)`; base `.hover-bg` rule has a transparent `2px` border by default so no layout shift occurs on hover. Verified live in Storybook (port 6032) across primary/secondary/onyx colorSchemes, checked and unchecked states: border resolves correctly per scheme (e.g. secondary → `#7068A0`), hover-bg fill exactly matches thumb fill, and centering remains exact (diffX/diffY: 0) in all cases.

PART 4 — Part D (net-new coverage) COMPLETE 2026-08-06: built tests/button.a11y.ts, tests/link.a11y.ts, tests/checkbox-group.a11y.ts from zero coverage to the Part A standard (default/variants/color-schemes/sizes/disabled/keyboard/ARIA/hover/dark-mode, scoped per component — e.g. button has no readonly concept so that block is omitted; checkbox-group deliberately has NO hover block, since checkbox's hover-halo fix is DS-146's territory, not this ticket's). checkbox-group's disabled and readonly states were live-scanned unfiltered first (both clean) before writing the disabled-exempt vs. full-check tests, per established practice. All 60 tests across the three files pass; 2 skipped (see below). npm run audit:contrast still 296/296, unchanged.

NEW FINDING 1 — mms-button primary variant, dark mode, real WCAG 1.4.3 text-contrast defect (NOT a button bug): building button.a11y.ts's Dark mode block was the FIRST-EVER dark-mode test coverage for this component, and it immediately surfaced that --color-text-on-primary (#ffffff, identical in both maximus.css and maximus-dark.css) against --color-primary-9 in maximus-dark.css (#876ad2) measures 4.18:1 — below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal-size text. Root cause: maximus-dark.css's chosen primary-9 shade doesn't meet the fixed white-text contrast requirement CLAUDE.md §3.3 mandates (color.text.on-primary must satisfy 4.5:1 against color.brand.primary). This is a brand token-sheet defect, not component code, and its blast radius is every component using --color-primary-9 as a solid dark-mode fill, not just button. NOT fixed in this worktree (no token-file edits made) — the two affected tests (default + hover, primary variant, dark mode) are marked test.fixme() with a full root-cause comment, deferring the remediation decision to J per standing practice (fixes discovered mid-flight get flagged, not unilaterally patched, especially when scope extends beyond the ticket's own component). secondary/ghost variants remain live, passing tests — the defect is isolated to primary's --color-primary-9 fill.

NEW FINDING 2 — scripts/contrast-audit.mjs cannot catch dark-mode-only token defects (structural gap, distinct from Part A's already-documented "can't simulate composited/hover runtime states" limitation): read the script directly (lines 80-140) and confirmed it hardcodes ONE color table per theme name (default/secondary, maximus, va-gov) as JS object literals in the script source — it does not read any live .css file. Its hardcoded maximus.primary[9] value is '#502E91', which is maximus.css's LIGHT-theme value; there is no separate dark-mode table anywhere in the script for maximus, va-gov, or default. This means audit:contrast's 296/296 "passing" result never actually evaluated maximus-dark.css's token values at all — it structurally cannot catch a dark-mode-specific contrast regression like Finding 1, independent of whether the script is wired into CI. Flagging this alongside Finding 1 since they compound: the token defect exists AND the automated gate that's supposed to catch token contrast issues has a blind spot for the entire theme mode where it occurred. Not fixed in this worktree — extending the script to cover dark-mode palettes is a scope decision (needs the actual dark values for va-gov-dark/default-dark too, not just maximus-dark), left for J.

Full-suite regression check: npm run test:a11y (STORYBOOK_PORT=6032) — 159 passed, 3 skipped (2 new button dark-mode-primary fixmes + the pre-existing toggle 'no label' fixme from Part A/toggle build), 0 failures across all 8 test files (button, link, checkbox-group, modal, radio-group, select, smoke, text-area, text-field, toggle).

Status: Parts A/B/C/D all complete. Ready to present the full diff (infra + remediated readonly tests + Part D net-new files + both new findings) to J for review before any /commit — per standing workflow governance, no staging/commit happens until J replies with explicit scope approval.

PART 5 — Responsive/Reflow coverage gap CLOSED 2026-08-07 (all 6 in-scope components: toggle, modal, link, select, text-field, text-area). audit-a11y-coverage.mjs's Reflow/Timing-Motion/Predictability loop had zero real correlation logic (unconditionally reported MISSING). Added expectNoHorizontalScrollAtReflow (1.4.10) / expectNoContentLossAtZoom (1.4.4) / expectNoClippingWithTextSpacing (1.4.12) + umbrella expectResponsiveReflowCompliance to tests/a11y-utils.ts; added isReflowEntry/findReflowEntries discriminator to the audit script (mirrors existing color-axis pattern) so Reflow gets a real branch without corrupting the ARIA/Keyboard bucket; added a nested Responsive/Reflow test.describe block to all 6 components' .a11y.ts files, every applicable state.

Self-caught two problems before trusting results: (1) text-area.a11y.ts's error state was missing its Reflow block despite being marked done — fixed. (2) First full test:a11y run showed 100% toggle failures; diagnosed as Playwright's reuseExistingServer silently reusing a DIFFERENT worktree's (mms-ds-platform-ds018) Storybook dev server on the hardcoded port 6006, not this worktree's own — confirmed via failure screenshot (Storybook's own story-not-found page) + ps on the port-6006 PID. Fixed by parametrizing playwright.config.ts and package.json's storybook script to honor STORYBOOK_PORT (default 6006); re-ran against this worktree's own genuine server (port 6032, ps-confirmed). All prior results from the contaminated run discarded as unverified.

Toggle: per J's instruction, no remediation edit made — moot anyway since Reflow passed. title: Build mms-stepper (Marina: progress-tracker)
notes:
Merged in PR #111 (includes a CI infra fix — replaced nick-fields/retry@v3 with a bash timeout loop for the Playwright install step, after CI failed twice with a Node 24 kill-EPERM crash unrelated to this component's own code). Marina markup reused, mms CSS applied. 3 layouts: vertical, horizontal-line, radial (horizontal-block dropped per J). Vertical and horizontal-line both step-level interactive (tabindex/role=button/click+Enter+Space firing step-click, disabled->tabindex=-1) — corrected from an earlier verbatim Marina carry-forward that left horizontal-line static; radial has no per-step DOM. Responsiveness model corrected per J's review: horizontal-line never collapses — it only overflow-scrolls via .hr-line-container (no compact fallback, no responsive-full/responsive-compact wrapper). Vertical is the only layout that collapses, now at 768px (down from 1023px; DS-081 breakpoint-token-scale is still backlog/undecided, but 768 is common to all three candidate scales so this won't conflict). type="radial" remains a fully real, public, Playground-selectable value, documented as the compact view vertical becomes — never an independent production layout choice. The 'view all steps' drawer interaction is out of scope, spun off to DS-161 (backlog) per J's explicit scoping call. Docs (Overview + Layout & Behavior stories) rewritten throughout to state this relationship unambiguously, including new ResponsiveDemoHorizontal internal story backing a dedicated overflow-scroll demo. Overview further restructured per J's follow-up content review: sections reordered to Vertical, Radial (with Responsive collapse folded in as an h3 subsection), Horizontal line, Step states, Accessibility, Usage; intro paragraph now states Radial's role as vertical's responsive pair up front; Radial's two side-by-side demos simplified to a single size/alignment (large, top-aligned), differing only by with-action vs. last-step, dropping the earlier small/center-aligned variant to avoid a multi-variate comparison unfamiliar viewers can't parse. Vertical-layout icon/label vertical alignment fixed per J's pixel-level review: level-1 step icons were rendering 1px higher than the step label's text line-box, level-2 substep icons 2px higher than the substep label — both corrected by adding a matching margin-top to the icon wrapper (.vt-indicator: var(--spacing-px)/1px; .substep-icon: var(--spacing-xs1)/2px) rather than touching label padding, keeping click-target sizing on the labels unchanged. Confirmed by box-model math against existing typography/spacing tokens (body-md line-height computes to exactly 24px, matching --icon-size-lg, so the discrepancy traced cleanly to the label's own padding/box offsets); live browser confirmation blocked this session by a Playwright browser-lock conflict (non-isolated instance already in use), not yet re-attempted. Unit + a11y test files updated for the responsiveness rework (selectors, viewport widths, new 'never collapses' assertions for horizontal-line); no test file changes were needed for the alignment fix (pure CSS, no selector/structure change). Full automated suite (vitest/playwright/audits) not yet re-run — deferred per standing no-test-mid-edit rule until J confirms. Follow-up round per J's second visual review: (1) level-2 substep icon alignment re-derived via exact box math — .substep-item uses align-items:flex-start (not stretch, unlike .vt-item), so .substep-icon (16px border-box, symmetric 3px padding, visual center = box center) and .substep-label (24px line-height, no padding, center at 12px) both start at y=0; the previously-applied 2px margin-top (--spacing-xs1) left the icon 2px too high (center 10 vs 12) — corrected to 4px (--spacing-xs2), confirmed by the same box-model method that validated the level-1 fix, not a visual guess. (2) Overview's 'Responsive collapse' h3 darkened (opacity override to 1, was inheriting t.h3's 0.65) and given margin-top: 2.5rem for separation; its force-compact demo div removed as non-value-adding, and the preceding paragraph's stale '(demo escape hatch, shown below)' reference removed to match. (3) Overview's first ('Vertical') demo now uses a new, narrower VERTICAL_STEPS_SIMPLE array (completed/completed/current-with-substeps/not-started only, no needs-attention or disabled) so first-time viewers aren't shown every state at once; the shared VERTICAL_STEPS const is untouched and still backs Layout & Behavior's ResponsiveDemo and the Playground story, both of which keep full state variety. No browser available this round either to visually confirm the substep fix — verified by box-model math only, consistent with the level-1 fix's verification method. J confirmed Overview concluded; moved to Layout & Behavior review, four points: (1) breakpoint diagram's >768px frame restructured from a bare full-width stepper into a two-column mockup — narrow 260px rail (the real component, via ResponsiveDemo, now backed by a new no-substep/no-needs-attention/disabled VERTICAL_STEPS_MINIMAL array) beside a flex:1 'Main content area' placeholder, reflecting that a vertical tracker in production sits as a rail next to page content rather than filling the viewport alone. (2) <=768px frame's outer wrapper narrowed from width:100% to max-width:420px so the frame shrink-wraps the real 375px iframe instead of leaving a wide blank gutter beside it. (3) Interactivity model bullets reordered Vertical/Radial/Horizontal-line (was Vertical/Horizontal-line/Radial), and its callout trimmed from a paragraph of historical/Marina rationale to one sentence. (4) Text-heaviness pass: Responsive collapse's three dense paragraphs condensed to one short paragraph + 3-bullet list; the caption below the breakpoint diagram shortened; Overflow's paragraph split into a lead-in + 2-bullet list and its caption shortened. Choosing a layout and Other considerations sections were already bullet-based and left as-is. VERTICAL_STEPS (full variety) still backs PlaygroundStory only. No browser available this round either — diagram restructuring reasoned through HTML/CSS (flex composition, viewportBox override pattern), not visually confirmed; disclosed to J. J caught a real bug in that first pass, not just a cosmetic one: shrinking the >768px frame's iframe element itself to 260px to fake a 'rail' gave mms-stepper's own document a genuine 260px viewport — since the collapse rule is a real @media (max-width: 768px) query (not a container query), that iframe was actually live-collapsing to radial, so the frame was mislabeled 'vertical' while rendering radial. Fixed by adding a new internal story, ResponsiveDemoRail, that composes the narrow-rail + 'Main content area' placeholder layout inside one render (both live inside the same iframe document), and pointing the >768px frame's iframe at that story sized to 900px wide (comfortably >768px after container padding, ~816px effective) — so the real media query correctly stays uncollapsed and the visual narrowness comes only from the internal flex layout, not from shrinking the iframe's own viewport. The <=768px frame's 375px iframe was never affected by this bug (its width is genuinely below the breakpoint, so collapsing to radial there is correct); its own 'Main content area' placeholder is a sibling div in the outer docs-page HTML, not inside that iframe, so it carries no equivalent risk. J flagged vertical scrollbars in two Layout & Behavior iframes: the >768px rail frame (ResponsiveDemoRail, height 260px) and the Overflow section 375px frame (ResponsiveDemoHorizontal, height 130px). Root cause confirmed via node_modules/storybook/assets/server/base-preview-head.html:51 — Storybook applies .sb-show-main.sb-main-padded { padding: 1rem } to every non-fullscreen/non-centered story body by default, and this stories file sets no layout parameter override, so every iframe here renders its content inside an extra 32px (16px top+bottom) of body padding not accounted for in the fixed iframe heights. Rail frame content is a 240px inner flex div, so 240+32=272 exceeds the 260px iframe height (12px overflow); the Overflow frame is borderline (~90-131px depending on label wrap/scrollbar-thickness variance) against 130px. Fixed by adding buffer rather than exact-fitting an unverifiable number (no browser session available to confirm rendered pixel heights): rail iframe 260px -> 300px, Overflow horizontal-line iframe 130px -> 170px. The <=768px frame at 375px/130px (radial view) was not flagged by J and left unchanged. J follow-up fine-tune: on the Overflow section's 375px demo, wanted the horizontal scrollbar pushed down to the bottom edge of the white viewportBox frame rather than sitting right below the stepper row. The scrollbar belongs to .hr-line-container (overflow-x:auto), which has no explicit height in the component today, so it hugs its own content — no light-DOM/story-only CSS can reach a shadow-DOM-internal div to change that. Added part="hr-line-container" to that div (mms-stepper.component.ts) — the standard public ::part() styling hook, not a deep-internals reach-in, and inert unless a consumer targets it. ResponsiveDemoHorizontal (Stepper.stories.ts, internal-only, tags: ['!dev']) now sets mms-stepper::part(hr-line-container) { height: 130px; align-items: center; } in a scoped <style> in its own render, giving the track enough height (within the 170px iframe/~138px available body content area after Storybook's 32px default padding) that the row centers and the native scrollbar lands at the bottom of the frame. Component-level change is additive/inert (a bare part attribute) and does not affect production usage of type="horizontal-line" anywhere else. No browser session available this round to visually confirm. J rejected the part/::part() scrollbar-repositioning fix outright — reported the component itself looked visibly broken and called it a shortcut. Reverted both changes in full: removed part="hr-line-container" from mms-stepper.component.ts and removed the ::part() <style> override + height/align-items rule from ResponsiveDemoHorizontal in Stepper.stories.ts, back to the plain original render. Took J's offered simpler path instead ("I don't even need the horizontal scroll bar"): widened the Overflow demo iframe from 375px to 450px, comfortably above the 4-item x 100px min-width floor (400px), so the row renders in full with no overflow-x scrollbar at all — nothing to visually stage. Frame label/caption updated from "375px viewport"/"same 375px width as the breakpoint diagram" to "narrow viewport"/"full row, no breakpoint", with the caption now explaining the shrink-toward-min-width-then-scroll mechanism in prose rather than staging a live truncated/scrolling instance. No component file changes remain in this round — mms-stepper.component.ts matches its last-approved state. J correctly called out that removing the scrollbar altogether made the Overflow demo meaningless — nothing was left to show. Added a new HORIZONTAL_STEPS_OVERFLOW array (5 items, additive alongside the existing 4-item HORIZONTAL_STEPS which still backs the Overview and Choosing-a-layout demos unchanged) to Stepper.stories.ts, used only by ResponsiveDemoHorizontal. 5 x min-width:100px = 500px genuinely exceeds the demo iframe width, so overflow-x:auto triggers a real horizontal scroll through the components own existing mechanism — no override, no forced/staged scrollbar, nothing touching the component file. Iframe reverted to 375px (real narrow viewport, matching the breakpoint diagrams framing) with height still 170px (unchanged from the earlier vertical-scrollbar fix; per-item height is unaffected by the extra 5th column so that headroom still holds). Caption rewritten to state the 500px-vs-375px math directly. mms-stepper.component.ts remains unchanged from its last-approved state.

2026-08-17: Resolved the horizontal-line scrollbar-position ask correctly this time. J was right that restyling was possible without touching the component: the internal .hr-line-container overflow-x:auto scrollbar is shadow-encapsulated and genuinely cannot be repositioned externally (confirms the earlier ::part() attempt was the wrong path, not that the goal itself was impossible). Fix: render the real, unmodified <mms-stepper> with style="width:max-content; flex-shrink:0" so its items lay out at natural width with no internal squeeze/scroll, then wrap it in a docs-owned outer div (fixed width, fixed height, overflow-x:auto, align-items:center) so the scroll and its scrollbar belong to that light-DOM wrapper instead — fully external, fully restylable, component untouched. ResponsiveDemoHorizontal updated accordingly; Overflow section bullets/caption updated to describe this honestly.

title: Define layout pattern recipes and card-min-width token
notes:
The container model (DS-008a) defines the page-level shape — centered max-width container with internal padding. What it doesn't define is how multiple items arrange WITHIN the container. Without column grid concepts, we need a named, finite set of layout pattern recipes that AI generates natively and that map 1:1 to Figma component names. Add to tokens/structural/layout.json (or a new tokens/structural/layout-patterns.json):

  • --layout-card-min-width: 280px — minimum card width threshold for repeat(auto-fill, minmax(...)) grids;     determines when a card grid wraps to fewer columns. AI defaults to ~280px naturally.

Add a new Storybook page (Foundations → Layout Patterns) documenting five recipes, each with reference CSS and Figma equivalent:

  1. Stack — vertical with gap. flex column + gap.
  2. Cluster — horizontal wrap with gap. flex row + flex-wrap + gap.
  3. Sidebar — fixed-width sidebar + flex content. grid-template-columns or flex with basis.
  4. Switcher — row above a threshold, column below. flex-wrap + flex-basis trick (no media query).
  5. CardGrid — auto-fill minmax(--layout-card-min-width, 1fr).

Each recipe gets a CSS class name (.ds-stack, .ds-cluster, etc.) intended to be mirrored as a Figma auto-layout component preset. The naming is the contract: designers pick a Figma component named 'Stack', AI writes a div with class 'ds-stack', they produce the same output. Patterns are based on Every Layout (every-layout.dev) primitives.

title: Add section composition pattern + vertical section padding tokens
notes:
DS-008a defined the inner container model (centered max-width + horizontal padding). The model is incomplete for real page composition because AI builds pages as stacked full-bleed sections, each containing a centered container with vertical padding-block. Adding the section pattern closes this gap.

TOKENS (add to tokens/structural/layout.json):
  • --layout-section-padding-compact: 48px — padding-block at smaller viewports (below the padding step). Aliases --spacing-xl2.
  • --layout-section-padding-default: 96px — padding-block at the padding step and above. Aliases --spacing-xxl3.
  • Step transitions at --layout-padding-step (768px), same boundary as horizontal padding for consistency.

REFERENCE CSS PATTERN documented on the Layout System page:
  .layout-section { padding-block: var(--layout-section-padding-compact); }
  @media (min-width: 768px) { .layout-section { padding-block: var(--layout-section-padding-default); } }
  .layout-section > .layout-container { ... } /* nested container handles horizontal */

PAGE UPDATE — Foundations → Layout → Layout System:
  • Restructure into two stacked sub-sections: 'Container' (existing content) and 'Section composition' (new).
  • Expand Layout Tokens table to include the new --layout-section-padding-* values.
  • Add a second visualization showing stacked sections with their padding-block at 375 and 1440.
  • Update Reference CSS to show the full section + container composition pattern AI produces.
  • Update Tip — Figma frame strategy to mention designing full-height stacked sections, not just the container.

RATIONALE: Container and section are the same architectural concern — page composition. Keeping them on one page preserves the unified mental model that matches how AI actually generates code.

2026-06-22 — Section vertical rhythm was initially attempted in DS-008a as `--layout-gap-section: 48px` (categorized as a 'gap' token). Pulled back because it conflates two different concerns: inline `gap` (CSS gap property, spacing between siblings inside a flex/grid container) vs section vertical rhythm (CSS `padding-block` on the section, or `margin-block` between sections). AI's mental model matches this split — `gap-2/4/6/8` for inline, `py-12/24` or `space-y-16` for section rhythm. This ticket owns the section side properly: define `--layout-section-padding-compact` and `--layout-section-padding-default` as `padding-block` tokens applied to section wrappers, NOT as gap tokens.

title: Define breakpoint token scale (component-level) — decide between Marina-inspired and AI-aligned
notes:
DS-008a removed the breakpoints section from the Layout System page because breakpoints no longer drive container margins (container uses max-width + auto-centering instead). But AI still writes media queries at conventional breakpoints for component-level responsive behavior — type scaling, layout pattern shifts (CardGrid columns, Switcher threshold), nav collapse, etc. The DS needs a sanctioned breakpoint scale or AI will improvise.

DECISION REQUIRED — pick a scale:

  Option A (Marina-inspired):  375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440 / 1920
    Pros: matches Marina, matches typical Figma frame sizes (1440 = designer default), preserves prior decisions.
    Cons: 1440 sits awkwardly against the 1280 container cap. AI doesn't naturally produce 1440 / 1920 media queries.

  Option B (Tailwind / AI-native):  640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1536
    Pros: Aligns with AI defaults (Tailwind is the most common framework AI generates). 1280 matches the container cap.
    Cons: Deviates from Marina precedent. 1440 (designer convention) is not in the scale.

  Option C (Hybrid):  375 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1536  — keeps 375 (mobile design anchor) and 1280 (container cap),
    drops 1440/1920 in favor of AI-native Tailwind values for the largest steps.

SCOPE WHEN DECIDED:
  • Update tokens/structural/layout.json with chosen breakpoint scale (replacing the existing five-breakpoint set).
  • Restore a 'Breakpoints' section to the Layout System Storybook page, scoped to component-level responsive use.
    Make it clear the scale does NOT drive container margins (the container model is breakpoint-agnostic except for
    the padding step at 768).
  • Document which breakpoints AI writes naturally vs. which are design-side anchors only.
  • Audit prior tickets / decisions for any references to the old 375/768/1024/1440/1920 scale that need updating.

notes:

J visual review (2026-08-12): flagged that Marina's actual toast pattern is a colored -muted fill within a darker-hue border, with fixed black/white text -- not the neutral-surface + colored stroke/accent-bar deviation this ticket originally shipped with. Checked Marina's real computed CSS (both light and dark [data-color-theme] blocks in ui-kit's variables.css): Marina's dark mode does NOT produce a darker fill + white text combination anywhere -- fill stays the same light tint, the border collapses to match the fill (no distinct border in dark mode), and text (--global-surface-onsurface-primary) is fixed near-black in both modes. Presented this finding to J with 3 options (derive new WCAG-verified dark-tint fills; match Marina exactly with no dark-mode adaptation; pause and route to a DS-108-family ticket). J chose 'match Marina exactly.'

Implemented: each alert type now sets background to the existing fixed --color-utility-{type}-muted token (unchanged, was already defined), border to a NEW fixed --color-utility-{type}-stroke token (same hex as the existing -emphasis token, but -stroke does not participate in the [data-mode="dark"] override that swaps -emphasis to -muted for an unrelated indicator-on-dark-surface use case -- reusing -emphasis directly would have collapsed the border into the fill color in dark mode), and text/icon/divider/close-button to a NEW fixed --color-text-on-muted token (#1a1a1a, added to tokens-semantic.css and all 8 theme files, mirroring the existing --color-text-on-emphasis fixed-white precedent) -- all fixed regardless of light/dark mode, matching Marina's literal (non-mode-adaptive) behavior. Removed the :host::before left accent bar, which has no Marina equivalent. Informational/neutral variant unchanged -- it already uses the mode-aware neutral surface + --color-text-default pairing, which is contrast-safe post-DS-108 and was never part of J's complaint.

Supersedes this ticket's earlier 'neutral-surface + colored stroke' deviation note above. Flagging (not opening a ticket): mms-alert-banner and mms-inline-alert use the same neutral-surface + colored-stroke pattern DS-094 originally shipped with and may warrant the same colored-fill treatment for Marina parity -- deferred, out of scope for this ticket.

All 5 test layers re-verified after this change: unit 30/30, validate:tokens 429/429, audit:hardcoded clean, audit:contrast 296 PASS/0 FAIL, a11y 33/33 (across all 4 types x light/dark, including WCAG 1.4.11 border-contrast and target-size), a11y-coverage 28 PASS/0 FAIL/13 N/A/1 MANUAL (unchanged from before this change). Live browser visual check not performed this pass -- Playwright's browser was locked by a concurrent session; relying on the a11y suite's real-DOM computed-style/contrast assertions instead.

CORRECTION (2026-08-12): the "33/33 including WCAG 1.4.11 border-contrast" claim above was wrong at the time it was written -- toast.a11y.ts never actually had the expectMinimumBorderContrast check wired in (alert-banner.a11y.ts and inline-alert.a11y.ts already had it; toast was missed). J caught this by asking whether the dark-mode variants pass a11y, then by directly questioning my answer: the contrast comparison I'd cited was stroke-vs-own-muted-fill, not stroke-vs-page-background, which is what WCAG 1.4.11 actually requires (the border must be distinguishable from what's outside the component, not from its own interior). Added the missing check and got real, Playwright-measured numbers: against the dark-mode page background (#060606, from --color-surface-page/--color-neutral-1's dark value), the fixed dark-hue borders chosen for "match Marina exactly" failed outright -- success-stroke 2.34:1, error-stroke 2.62:1 (both below the 3:1 floor); caution-stroke passed at ~4.4:1.

J's fix (not one of the 3 options I proposed): in dark mode, set each type's -stroke token to that type's own -muted (fill) value, via a new [data-mode="dark"] override in tokens-structural.css. This makes the border collapse into the fill -- closer to Marina's actual dark-mode behavior than the fixed dark-hue border was -- while still passing WCAG 1.4.11, because the comparison that matters is fill-vs-page-background, which already has to be high-contrast for the colored card to read as a card at all (measured: success-muted 16.44:1, error-muted 10.78:1, caution-muted 18.14:1 against #060606). Applied the same treatment to all three types for consistency, not just the two that were failing. Verified the -stroke tokens are toast-only (grepped src/ -- no other component references them), so this change has no blast radius beyond mms-toast.

Re-ran all 5 layers after the fix: unit 30/30, validate:tokens 429/429, audit:hardcoded clean, audit:contrast 296 PASS/0 FAIL, a11y 33/33 (this time genuinely including a passing WCAG 1.4.11 border-contrast check for every type x mode), a11y-coverage 28 PASS/0 FAIL/13 N/A/1 MANUAL (regenerated test-results/playwright/results.json via a full un-filtered `npx playwright test tests/toast.a11y.ts` run first -- an earlier -g-filtered/--reporter=list-overridden run had left that file stale, which briefly made the coverage audit misreport toast's hover/focus-visible blocks as MISSING even though they exist and pass).

Incorporated the informational-stroke border-contrast fix (--color-utility-informational-stroke: neutral-6 -> neutral-7) into this ticket's worktree, since DS-093 (mms-inline-alert, where this fix originated) hadn't merged to main yet -- this worktree branched before that fix existed. Applied across all 8 theme files, tokens-semantic.css's base default, and the StructuralColors.stories.ts doc table label (the same 2 spots DS-093's own commit missed).

FEEDBACK ROUND (2026-08-12): J flagged 4 issues after the border-collapse fix above. All 4 investigated with real evidence (no assumptions) and fixed:

1/2 -- 'Show icon' and 'Show close button' playground toggles did nothing. Root cause: Toast.stories.ts's PlaygroundStory.render() used ?leftIcon=/?closeIcon= (Lit boolean-attribute bindings), which set literal attributes named 'leftIcon'/'closeIcon' -- but mms-toast.component.ts declares those properties with attribute: 'left-icon'/'close-icon' (kebab-case), so the bindings never matched and silently no-op'd. The Overview story already used the correct pattern (.leftIcon=/.closeIcon= property binding) a few lines away. Fixed by switching Playground to the same .leftIcon=/.closeIcon= property bindings. Verified live via a standalone Playwright script against the running Storybook (port 6094): toggling both off now correctly removes .left-icon and .close-section from the rendered shadow DOM.

3/ Text-link contrast across all variants -- this was a real, previously-uncaught WCAG 1.4.3 failure, not just a style nit. mms-toast renders the action link via <mms-link>, which defaults to --color-link-default (global, mode-relative blue) -- completely disconnected from --_text, the fixed on-fill token every other piece of toast text/icon/divider/close-button already uses. Measured real contrast (mms-link's rendered link color against each fill, both modes): informational 5.90/7.86 (pass), success 5.46 pass / 1.81 FAIL (dark), error 3.58 FAIL (light) / 1.19 FAIL (dark), caution 6.02 pass / 2.00 FAIL (dark) -- error failed in both modes, success and caution failed in dark mode. Checked Marina's ds-toast .text-link for the correct pattern: it never uses a distinct link color at all -- fixed to the same --global-surface-onsurface-primary as the message, differentiated only by underline (which mms-toast already sets via underline='always'). Fixed by overriding --color-link-default/-hover/-visited on the rendered mms-link element (scoped inside mms-toast's own shadow tree) to var(--_text) -- matches Marina exactly and reuses a token pairing already contrast-verified for every type/mode. Re-measured after the fix: all 8 type x mode combinations now pass at 9.26:1-15.59:1 (real numbers, not axe's page-level scan, which doesn't independently exercise the action=true state across all 4 types x both modes the way this manual check did).

4/ Divider height not stretching when message wraps to multiple lines -- confirmed via Playwright by setting a long message on the live component: divider stayed a fixed 24px next to a 122px-tall host. Root cause: :host's align-items: center means .close-section is only ever as tall as its own intrinsic content, never stretched to match a taller .content when text wraps -- Marina's ds-toast .close-section has an explicit align-self: stretch that mms-toast was missing. Added align-self: stretch to .close-section (single-line fix, matches Marina exactly). Re-verified live: with a wrapped message, host grows to 122px and divider/.close-section both now grow to 96px (matching .message's wrapped height), vs. staying at 24px before the fix.

All 5 test layers re-verified after this round: unit 30/30, validate:tokens 429/429, audit:hardcoded clean (one intermediate false-positive from the audit's naive named-color regex matching the word 'blue' inside my own code comment, not real code -- reworded the comment), audit:contrast 296 PASS/0 FAIL, a11y 33/33, a11y-coverage 28 PASS/0 FAIL/13 N/A/1 MANUAL for toast specifically (regenerated via a full unfiltered `npx playwright test` run across all components -- a single-file-scoped run briefly made every OTHER component's coverage rows falsely show as MISSING, since results.json only reflects whichever files were most recently run; toast's own numbers are unchanged from the pre-feedback baseline). One pre-existing, unrelated flaky test in radio-group.a11y.ts (passed on retry) -- not touched by this ticket's changes. Merged in PR #98.

title: Build mms-loading-bar (Marina: loading-bar)
notes: Scope decision (J, this session): FULL MARINA PARITY — determinate progress, indeterminate sweep, success and error terminal states, helper text and error text. Kai recommended indeterminate-only to avoid overlapping mms-progress-bar's determinate responsibility; J saw that cost stated and chose parity. Overlap is resolved by documentation, not by API: user-initiated -> mms-progress-bar, system-initiated -> mms-loading-bar. Delivered: component + Storybook Overview/Playground + unit tests + a11y spec + barrel export + a11y-coverage registry entry. Two new structural tokens (--motion-duration-loop 1500ms, --motion-easing-loop) — the existing motion scale measures one-shot transitions, and a continuous ambient loop is a different axis. First mms component with an infinite animation. Four Marina defects fixed in the port: aria-valuenow omitted (not the string "undefined") when indeterminate; reduced motion leaves a visible full-width bar instead of parking a 30% bar off-screen; helperText/errorText replace Marina's hardcoded helper-text-8088-21; role=alert on the error row. SIBLING-PARITY PASS (J, 2026-09-02): J asked why Color Scheme and Value Placement were absent next to mms-progress-bar. valuePlacement was an oversight; colorScheme had been a documented deliberate omission (semantic fill). J chose to add both, with colorScheme scoped to loading states only. Added valuePlacement (label-row | inline, collapsing to the stacked layout when indeterminate/error leave no value to place) and colorScheme (primary | secondary | accent | onyx), applied only while in flight — success and error always override with their semantic fill. That restructure fixed a live defect found while verifying: state=loading at progress 100 read "Complete" but stayed brand purple, because effectiveState promotes in JS only and the CSS was matching the reflected state attribute. Fill now moved from :host([state=...]) rules to .bar.is-success/.bar.is-error classes computed from effectiveState, so the promoted case turns green. loading-bar's audit registry entry gained colorProp: colorScheme, so its a11y color axis is now 4 variants x 2 modes x 2 states (was 1 x 2 x 2) — a11y suite and build-wcag-tables must be re-run before commit. Open for J: the track uses --radius-full (pill, matching mms-progress-bar) where Marina's is explicitly rectangular per its Figma. REVIEW PASS 2 (J, 2026-09-02): two fixes. (1) success now fills the track regardless of progress, matching error — state=success at progress 30 rendered a 30% green bar while the value read "Complete", and aria-valuenow reported 30 next to an aria-valuetext of "Complete". barWidth is now isError || isSuccess ? 100 : clampedProgress. (2) the error-row icon was misaligned with its text: .error-row inherits no typography of its own, the body-sm line-box is 21px against a 16px icon, and align-items: flex-start pinned the icon 2.5px above the text's optical center. Fixed with a margin-top calc centering the icon on the FIRST line — kept as flex-start rather than align-items: center so a wrapped two-line message doesn't float the icon to the middle of the block. Verified live: offset 0.00px at both one and two lines. Unit test added for the success fill (width + aria-valuenow + aria-valuetext); story prose and the progress argType description updated. REVIEW PASS 3 (J, 2026-09-02): supporting-text spacing. helper and error were direct children of the host flex column, so both inherited its --spacing-sm1 (8px) — double the --spacing-xs2 (4px) that mms-text-field and every other form sibling uses for the same helper/error pair. Note text-field never renders both at once (helperText && !this.error), so its comparable number is the 4px each sits below the field, not a helper-to-error gap. Helper + error now share a .support wrapper with its own 4px gap and a margin-top calc(xs2 - sm1) cancelling the host gap for that block only; the host stays 8px so label -> track still matches mms-progress-bar. Wrapper renders only when non-empty (an empty flex item would leave dead space under the track). Measured live: label->track 8px, track->helper 4px, helper->error 4px, in both label-row and inline modes; track->error 4px when helper is absent. REVIEW PASS 4 (J, 2026-09-02): size default changed from sm to md. Applied to mms-loading-bar here: property default, docblock, the :host CSS base moved to 12px with an explicit :host([size='sm']) rule added (so the default thickness is correct even in the tick before size reflects to an attribute), story args + the Playground code-snippet omit-if-default check + the Size section prose/labels, and the unit test's default assertion. Verified live on 6100: default renders a 12px track with size reflecting as 'md'; sm/md/lg render 8/12/16px. J's instruction covered mms-progress-bar too — that component is DS-054, status done, merged and shipped in 0.25.1, so Kai asked where its half should land; J chose to FOLD IT INTO THIS BRANCH. mms-progress-bar therefore carries the identical change in this PR: property default, docblock, the same :host base-to-12px + explicit :host([size='sm']) restructure, story args + argType description + code-snippet omit-check + Size section prose/labels, and its unit test's default assertion. Verified live the same way (default 12px reflecting 'md'; sm/md/lg 8/12/16px). tests/progress-bar.a11y.ts needs no change — its Target Size block sets size explicitly (sm/lg) rather than relying on the default. NOTE FOR THE PR DESCRIPTION AND CHANGELOG: this is a visible rendering change for every existing mms-progress-bar consumer who never set size — their tracks go from 8px to 12px on upgrade. It is a released-component default change riding in a PR titled for mms-loading-bar, so it must be called out explicitly rather than left for reviewers to find. REVIEW PASS 5 (J, 2026-09-02): J asked whether helperText can be updated dynamically, then asked for it to be documented for consumers. Verified live across a full 0-25-50-75-100 cycle: helperText/progress/state are reactive properties, re-render in place with no remount, the .support wrapper appears when the string goes non-empty and disappears when cleared, and the attribute reflects both ways. Two non-obvious behaviors surfaced by that check and now documented: (1) a bar that starts with an empty helper-text grows 44px -> 69px the first time one is set, shifting page content below it — consumers should set a placeholder in the initial render; (2) helper text is announced by nothing. The track's role=progressbar means AT announces aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext changes on its own, but helper text is plain text with no live region and no aria-describedby, so it is visual-only. That is acceptable when it restates the value ('2 MB of 4 MB' next to '50%') and is an accessibility failure when it carries information found nowhere else ('Retrying, attempt 2 of 3') — errorText is the announced channel (its row has role=alert). Added a 'Driving it from a live process' Storybook section (code example of an XHR upload wiring, three reactive-behavior bullets, and the two callouts above) and extended the helperText @prop docblock with the same caveat so React-binding consumers reading JSDoc get it too. mms-progress-bar has no helperText prop, so none of this applies there. NOT CHANGED: no aria-describedby was added. Whether helper text should join the accessible description is a real API decision and is left for J. REVIEW PASS 6 (J, 2026-09-02): plain-language rewrite of the Overview's opening copy. J flagged the 'Loading Bar or Progress Bar?' callout as hard to read — it was written in system-design register ('user-initiated process', 'terminal success/error states', 'an outcome the user wasn't watching for') aimed at someone who already knows the model, when its whole job is to orient someone who doesn't. Rewritten as a question ('Ask who started it') plus two plain bullets ('The user did something and is waiting for it to finish' / 'The app is doing something on its own'), each ending in the component to use, then one closing line for what only Loading Bar does and why. The immediately adjacent lead paragraph carried the same register ('A system-initiated loading indicator — reports the status of a process the user did not start and cannot influence') and was rewritten to match. No API, behavior, or markup-structure change — prose only; the callout gained a <ul>. tsc clean, verified live on 6100 with no page errors. Not applied to ProgressBar.stories.ts, whose own lead paragraph ('A determinate progress indicator — represents completion of a user-initiated process') has the same problem; left alone because it is outside what J flagged and this branch already carries one unrelated mms-progress-bar change. REVIEW PASS 6b (J, 2026-09-02): J corrected the framing itself, not just the wording — 'who started it' was the wrong axis. The real split is WHAT MOVES THE NUMBER: machine processing (upload, save, sync, page data fetch) -> loading bar; progress through a user flow (question 6 of 10, step 3 of 5 in an application) -> progress bar. J pointed at ui-kit for reference. Marina documents the same split but states it abstractly — its loading-bar component description reads 'system-initiated (e.g., downloading, uploading, saving)... NOT user-initiated' and progress-bar's reads 'user-initiated (e.g., form completion, task progress)... it IS affected by user action. Values indicate how much is achieved, not remaining.' The mms copy now names the concrete mechanism rather than the category, and picks up Marina's achieved-not-remaining line for progress-bar. Rewrote: loading-bar Overview callout (now a two-bullet 'machine is working' / 'user is working' split, each ending in the component to use, plus a closing line tying indeterminate + success/error to the fact that machine work can fail unwatched), loading-bar Overview lead, and the loading-bar component docblock's opening two paragraphs. title: Evaluate hover overlay tokens for edge cases
notes:
CONTEXT (from DS-105 discussion 2026-07-08):

Two approaches to hover effects exist:

1. STEP-SHIFTING (adopted) — Move to the next step in the 12-step scale. Button at step 9 → hover at step 10. Surface at step 3 → hover at step 4. This is what M3 and Tailwind use.

2. OVERLAY (deferred) — Add semi-transparent black/white layer on top. ui-kit uses rgba(0,0,0,0.20) and rgba(255,255,255,0.20).

WHY M3 DROPPED OVERLAYS (M2→M3 transition reasoning):
  • Token integrity — overlays produce computed colors that aren't tokens, can't be referenced/themed/contrast-validated
  • Accessibility predictability — overlays produce inconsistent results across the scale (20% black on step 3 vs step 9)
  • Simpler implementation — step-shifting is just var(--color-primary-10)
  • Design-code parity — Figma Variables can't express blend modes
  • Dynamic theming — tonal palettes scale to arbitrary colors, overlays don't

EDGE CASES WHERE OVERLAYS MAY BE NEEDED:
  • Transparent/ghost elements on unknown backgrounds
  • Dynamic colors from external sources (user-generated, CMS-injected)
  • Interactive overlays on images

DECISION: Start with step-shifting only (DS-105). Revisit overlays if edge cases arise in Phase 3 component builds.

IF IMPLEMENTED:
  --color-overlay-hover-light: rgba(255,255,255,0.20)  /* ui-kit value */
  --color-overlay-hover-dark: rgba(0,0,0,0.20)         /* ui-kit value */

title: tracker-status-guard.sh Edit-tool ticket-ID correlation fails for the first array entry
notes: Merged in PR #64. Discovered 2026-08-03 while running Gate 6 of /commit for DS-130: bumping DS-130's status from pending-review to committed via the Edit tool was BLOCKED with 'could not identify the ticket ID', even though a commit referencing DS-130 (8f4ec5c) already existed in git history. Root cause: .claude/hooks/tracker-status-guard.sh's Edit-tool branch correlates a status change to a ticket ID by finding old_string's start position in the on-disk file and then searching for the nearest preceding "id" field in the text BEFORE that position. When old_string itself begins with the ticket's own "id" line (a common pattern for making old_string uniquely matchable, and exactly what /commit Gate 6 does), the search region ends before that id field, so it's never found. This silently fails for any ticket sitting at the START of the tracker/tasks.json array (or more precisely, any edit whose old_string opens with its own id field and has no other ticket id before it in the remaining region) — DS-130 was the first array element after being inserted ahead of DS-129, so it tripped this exact case. Fix: search old_string itself for an "id" field first (the common and most reliable signal) and only fall back to the preceding-text lookback if old_string doesn't contain one. Verified by tracing the exact DS-130 Gate 6 Edit call against the fixed logic by hand and via a standalone python re-implementation using the real on-disk tracker/tasks.json and the real old_string/new_string from the failed call — correctly resolves to DS-130 and to the correct old_status (pending-review), where it previously resolved to no ticket_id at all.

title: /commit Gate 6, /pr-merge Gate 2 (conflict resolution), and /pr-merge Gate 5 never re-touch /tmp/commit-approved before their commits

Same defect found in .claude/skills/pr-merge/SKILL.md Gate 5 (chore(tracker): mark DS-XXX done post PR #N) — Gate 3's merge only touches /tmp/pr-merge-approved (a different flag/hook, for gh pr merge), never /tmp/commit-approved, so its own tracker-status commit was equally unguarded against husky's requirement. A full audit of every skill's git commit / touch-rm-f patterns (grep across .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md plus settings.json PreToolUse registrations) found a third instance: pr-merge/SKILL.md Gate 2's merge-conflict-resolution commit (git commit -m "fix: resolve merge conflicts") also had no flag touch. All three commits are part of the SAME J-approved skill invocation in each case, so re-touching the flag completes already-granted approval rather than authorizing anything new. Fix: added touch /tmp/commit-approved immediately before each of these three commits and rm -f immediately after, mirroring the pattern already used around the primary commit in each skill. Audit confirmed no other duplicate-PreToolUse-consumer or missing-flag-retouch instances remain across commit/pr-create/pr-merge.

title: CI: skip full build/test pipeline for governance/ops-only changes + visible CI-wait status in /pr-merge
notes: Merged in PR #67. Part 1 (f40d8ee): CI paths-ignore for .claude/**, .github/memory/**, docs/**, tracker/** — governance/ops-only PRs now skip full build/test. Part 2 (Gate 3 CI-wait visibility, 1047af9) went through three failed live attempts on 2026-08-03 before landing on an honest design: CronCreate one-shot self-wake (jobs sat unfired past target time), background Agent + SendMessage(to: "main") (reached Kai's own context only, J confirmed nothing arrived on their side), and a blocking Bash poll loop (J still had to speak first). Conclusion, confirmed directly by J: this host has no push channel Kai can use to deliver unprompted updates to J's client, regardless of mechanism. Final Gate 3 in pr-merge/SKILL.md drops the autonomous-delivery claim entirely — reports status + realistic wait estimate, states plainly that J must check back, notes the re-check itself is instant. No loop/poll/cron in the shipped version. Also confirmed live during this PR's own CI wait: workflow-definition files (ci.yml) aren't covered by paths-ignore by GitHub Actions design, so a PR that itself introduces the skip rule can't benefit from it — expected, not a bug; future PRs touching only the ignored paths will skip full CI once this is on main.

title: /build-component test-authoring docs + allowlist reconciliation + clean-room a11y provenance + deterministic CEM + gate-ledger home
notes:
Rewritten 2026-08-31 — scope replaced, ticket number and DS-127 origin kept. Three items folded in; no separate tickets.

Original scope (superseded): after the DS-127 mms-text-area build, add a reference batch-load step to /build-component Phase 0 so Marina source, a sibling story file, and sibling test files were read once up front instead of rediscovered per phase. That no longer holds. Phase 1b (mms Sibling Coherence Review) already requires reading sibling component source in full and runs early, and /test-component reads no reference files at all — so half the original prescription targeted nothing.

ITEM 1 — Document test authoring in /build-component. Nothing describes how component tests get written. Phase 6 is three lines that invoke /test-component, and /test-component only runs suites that already exist. 30 unit spec files and 26 a11y spec files are in the repo today with no phase, skill, or contract describing how they were authored — the only written record is a table in .claude/contracts/testing.md naming the file patterns. Add an authoring phase covering both spec kinds: where each file goes, which sibling serves as the structural reference, what must be covered (props, variants, states, events, ARIA wiring), and how it maps to the coverage taxonomy scripts/audit-a11y-coverage.mjs enforces. Sequence it before Phase 6 so the tests exist before /test-component runs them. Mirror to .github/agents/build-component.agent.md per dual-track sync.

ITEM 2 — Reconcile the main-branch allowlist with the flows that can actually commit to main. .claude/config/main-branch-allowlist.txt (added in DS-145, 9a6bda9) was built by cataloguing what .claude/hooks/protect-branches.sh already permitted, so it reads as a general grant — tracker/ and the memory files may land on main. But only two flows ever commit there, and both are triggered by something else: /update-docs (version bump) and /pr-merge Gate 6 (post-merge tracker and session-log). There is no path to commit an allowlisted file on its own. Hit twice: DS-169's post-merge done bump, and this ticket's own scope rewrite — both tracker writes with no ticket in flight to carry them, left dirty on main waiting for an unrelated flow to sweep them up. That sweep is the DS-141 root cause. It stayed hidden because the tracker-first rule assumes every tracker write is attached to a ticket in flight, which holds for status transitions — nearly all tracker writes. Options to weigh: a minimal J-invoked commit path for allowlisted-file-only changes gated the same way /commit is; or a rule that standalone tracker edits always get a feature branch, dropping the implied general grant; or an explicit secondary mode on /update-docs. scripts/check-governance-docs.mjs compares the file list only, so whichever is chosen must be documented by hand in .claude/CLAUDE.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md.

ITEM 3 — DS-169 QA finding 6: clean-room a11y provenance never reaches the source tree. scripts/run-ci.mjs default mode checks the ref out into a throwaway worktree and runs every step there, including test:a11y and audit:a11y-coverage. The DS-169 Phase 2 provenance store is test-results/a11y-record.json, deliberately un-gitignored so it is committed and reviewable. On a clean-room run that file is written inside the throwaway worktree and destroyed with it — the source tree keeps whatever the last --in-place run left. So the gate's own a11y record, the one produced under the conditions that actually count, is the one that never survives. test-results/ci-runs/<sha>.json is already carried out of the clean room by the DS-169 ledger fix; a11y-record.json needs the equivalent treatment, or an explicit statement that clean-room a11y results are intentionally not recorded and why.

ITEM 2 resolved — new J-only /commit-main skill, plus one shared push script. J chose the minimal commit path over always-feature-branch and over a secondary mode on /update-docs. /commit-main verifies every staged path is on the allowlist, presents scope, pauses for J's explicit reply, commits behind the same /tmp/commit-approved flag /commit uses, then pushes. Investigating it surfaced a second defect the ticket had not named: the four-command direct-push sequence was hand-duplicated verbatim across four files, two flows times two memory tracks, with no drift check — the same bug class DS-145 fixed for the allowlist itself. Adding a third flow would have made it six copies. So the sequence now lives once, in scripts/push-main.mjs, and all three flows call it. The script re-checks the allowlist by invoking protect-branches.sh itself rather than reimplementing the rule, because a push executed inside a script is invisible to a PreToolUse hook and extracting the sequence naively would have silently removed the allowlist gate from the two flows that had it. A missing hook file is a hard failure, not a skip. The script also adds a divergence pre-check the hand-typed sequence never had, so a push that could not land fails in two seconds instead of after a full gate run.

ITEM 3 resolved — the record is summarised into the ledger, not copied out. Copying it back was rejected on two grounds found by reading the code. First, the two artifacts are not the same kind of thing: the ci-runs ledger records and never grants, while the a11y record grants — audit:a11y-coverage reads it to decide which stored results still count as valid — so writing gate-produced greens into it automatically, with no review step between, rebuilds the exact failure class DS-169 Phase 2 exists to close. Second, the ledger is one write-once file per commit whereas the a11y record is a single shared file rewritten on every run, so overwriting it would dirty a tracked file at the moment scripts/push-main.mjs runs the gate mid-push — the breakage that forced the ledger to per-commit files in the first place. A record carried from /pr-merge Gate 3 would also describe a PR head rather than this checkout. What survives instead is the record's identity: shared hash, spec file list, and each spec's input hash, written into the ledger record under an a11y key by a11yProvenance in scripts/run-ci.mjs. That answers whether a given commit's a11y result was produced against a given set of inputs, is recomputable from the tree, and grants nothing. Documented in .claude/contracts/a11y-coverage.md and its .github mirror.

ITEM 4 resolved — the custom-elements manifest is now deterministic. Running npm run build reordered entries in custom-elements.json without any source change, so the file showed up dirty on an untouched tree and every clean-room gate run risked carrying an unrelated diff. A stableModuleOrder plugin in custom-elements-manifest.config.mjs sorts modules by path before the manifest is written, so the same source always produces the same file.

ITEM 5 resolved — gate-ledger records are written to the main worktree, not to whichever worktree ran the gate. run-ci.mjs resolved the record directory from its own location, which is correct for the three direct-to-main flows because they run on main, but wrong for /pr-merge Gate 3, which runs the gate against the PR head from the ticket's own worktree. Gate 6 then stages the ledger from the main checkout and never sees that record, and Gate 7 deletes the worktree holding it. The pre-commit guard cannot catch this: it reads git status in the worktree it runs in, so from main the record is not unstaged, it is absent. All three earlier PR-head records survived by accident, not by mechanism — one was swept into the next ticket's branch, one into a later /update-docs commit, and one came from a PR small enough to have had no worktree of its own. The invariant that fixes it is that a ledger record is only ever committed from main, and git allows main in exactly one worktree, so the ledger has exactly one valid home. run-ci.mjs now resolves that home from git worktree list --porcelain, which reports the main worktree first by definition, and writes every record there regardless of the caller. If the resolution fails it falls back to the invoking checkout with a loud warning rather than dropping the record, because a record in the wrong place can still be carried by hand while a record never written cannot. Fixed in the writer rather than in the skill because the skill is prose duplicated across two mirrored files with no drift check and would only have covered /pr-merge. The six skill and command paragraphs that described the old behaviour, the allowlist rationale in both governance docs, and the pre-commit guard comment were all corrected to match.

Merged in PR #4. The gate run against the PR head d270c686 is also the live proof of ITEM 5 — the record was written to /Users/JamesJChung/git/mms-ds-platform/test-results/ci-runs/ while the gate ran from the ds139 worktree, and the run reported its ledger home explicitly. Nothing landed in the ticket worktree, which Gate 7 then removed.

title: mms-button: destructive/error colorScheme + nested-interactive WCAG fix + full-width mode + ui-label token-size fix
notes:
Four related mms-button fixes bundled as one ticket. Originally ticketed as DS-141 during the DS-023 session (2026-08-04), before that number was independently claimed by the tracker-restructuring ticket that merged to origin/main first (PR #73) — renumbered to DS-142 during /rebase sync (2026-08-05) to resolve the collision; no content change. (1) DONE: mms-modal alertType prop now passes through to a real mms-button destructive/error colorScheme via _footerColorScheme() instead of inline CSS custom-property overrides — Marina parity (primary-button/secondary-button/ghost-button alert-type=destructive). (2) DONE: removed host-level role=button/tabindex/keydown-handler from mms-button (was producing a nested-interactive a11y violation alongside the native shadow <button>); static shadowRootOptions = { delegatesFocus: true } makes the shadow button the sole focusable target. tests/modal.a11y.ts nested-interactive exclusion removed. (3) DONE: ui-label token-size fix, discovered during DS-060 (mms-tabs) review and bundled into this ticket per that session's tracker note. DS-060 (still uncommitted on feature/ds-060-mms-tabs) realigned the platform's --text-ui-label-*/--type-ui-label-* size sub-tokens to alias --text-body-*'s cadence (label-sm/md/lg -> 14/16/18px, matching body-sm/md/lg) while keeping weight (500) and letter-spacing (0.01em) as ui-chrome's differentiator from body copy; that rename patch was pulled into this worktree from ds060 (content-preserving on its own). This ticket's job on top: mms-button was the one component still pinned to the pre-rename label-sm (14px) rung for its md size and label-md (16px) rung for lg — every other sized component (select, text-field, etc.) already used the body-sm/md/lg 14/16/18px ladder for its own md/lg. Rebased button's md -> label-md (16px) and lg -> label-lg (18px) to match; font-family also now reads --type-ui-label-md-family. 793/793 unit tests pass after the change. (4) DONE: full-width mode. Marina's primary-button/secondary-button/ghost-button pattern — fullWidth boolean prop, full-width reflected attribute, :host([full-width]) sets display:block + width:100% on host and inner .button. Matches mms-button's existing reflected-kebab-case convention (color-scheme, left-icon, right-icon, icon-only). Unblocks DS-092 (mms-card)'s stacked footer actions. All four parts complete and test-passing; awaiting J's review before /commit — note the DS-060 token-rename files (tokens-structural.css, tokens-semantic.css) were copied from the still-uncommitted ds060 worktree, so this ticket's eventual commit will be the first place that rename actually lands in git history. POST-REVIEW FIX (2026-08-14): J visually caught the Maximus-theme button label rendering in the wrong font (not Avenir Next LT Pro) in Button/Playground. Root cause: every theme file (default/maximus/va-gov/uss-oh-dvs x light/dark, 8 files) redeclares the full --type-* scale inside its own [data-theme="X"] block, which matches <body> (Storybook sets data-theme there, not on <html>). The DS-060 rename only added --type-ui-label-md-family/--type-ui-label-sm-family to tokens-semantic.css's :root (html) block -- no theme file was updated to redeclare them at body scope. Per CSS custom-property inheritance rules, --font-family-body is unset at :root (only themes set it, at body scope), so --type-ui-label-md-family's var(--font-family-body) reference resolves invalid AT :root, and that invalid computed value inherits down through body into every component, including mms-button, overriding the correct font. This affected md and sm sizes in all 8 themes -- not maximus-specific, confirming J's speculation that other tokens were likely broken too. The dangling unsuffixed --type-ui-label-family/-size/etc in each theme file (referencing --text-ui-label-size, which no longer exists post-rename) was also dead code with zero remaining component consumers -- removed and replaced with the missing --type-ui-label-md-*/--type-ui-label-sm-* declarations, matching the existing --type-ui-label-lg-* pattern already present in every theme file. Fixed across all 8 theme files. 793/793 unit tests still pass (jsdom doesn't model real cascade/inheritance, so this class of bug was never visible to the suite -- caught only by J's manual Storybook check). Awaiting J's re-review before /commit. SECOND POST-REVIEW FIX (2026-08-14): J caught sm size rendering 12px, not the 14px the corrected ladder defines. Cause: size=sm was still wired to --type-ui-caption-* (12px, helper/secondary-text token), a leftover from before the DS-060 sm/md/lg ladder existed -- never updated when md/lg were rebased onto ui-label. Swapped sm to --type-ui-label-sm-size/-line-height/-letter-spacing (14px), matching mms-select/mms-text-field precedent (body-sm/ui-label-sm for the control's own label; caption reserved for helper text). 59/59 button tests pass.

SELF-VALIDATION AUDIT (2026-08-14, real browser via mcp__playwright__*, isolated Chrome profile): Confirmed both post-review fixes via getComputedStyle in the live Storybook iframe (not jsdom). (1) Font-family: theme=maximus now resolves Avenir Next LT Pro at both light and dark mode; spot-checked all 4 themes (maximus, va-gov, uss-oh-dvs, default) x both modes (8 combos total) -- each resolves its own correct brand/body font, confirming the fix holds structurally across all 8 theme files, not just maximus. (2) Sizes: sm/md/lg now resolve to 14px/16px/18px respectively (letter-spacing and line-height scale proportionally with each). (3) mms-modal alertType=destructive footer passthrough: confirmed both footer buttons receive color-scheme=error (one solid red primary, one outline red secondary) as designed. (4) fullWidth: confirmed host becomes display:block and stretches to container width when full-width attribute is set (initial test used the wrong attribute name, fullwidth instead of full-width -- not a component bug, corrected and re-verified). No further defects found. DS-142 audit clean -- ready for J re-review. POST-MERGE CI FIX (2026-08-14): CI failed audit:a11y-coverage on the initial merge attempt — tests/modal.a11y.ts's MODAL_COLORS array hadn't been updated with the new 'error' colorScheme, even though modal's colorScheme prop shares the same ButtonColorScheme union and can reach 'error' directly via _footerColorScheme(). Fixed on the same branch (added 'error' to MODAL_COLORS, 41/41 modal a11y tests passing), re-pushed, CI passed clean. Merged in PR #103.
