title: Add .github/agents/** to ci.yml paths-ignore
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-31 — moot, superseded by DS-169. Not implemented; nothing to implement. Closure merged in PR #3 (status stays `removed`, not `done` — nothing was built). The target file `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was deleted in 403816b when the repo migrated to maximus-atx-ce, where GitHub Actions is disabled at the enterprise level. `.github/workflows/` no longer exists. CI is now local (`scripts/run-ci.mjs`, `npm run ci`) and has no path-filtering mechanism of any kind — every run executes the full step suite regardless of which files changed, so there is no paths-ignore list to add `.github/agents/**` to.

The underlying idea should not be ported forward either. run-ci.mjs:156-163 documents the cost of the old paths-ignore directly: because ci.yml ignored `.claude/**` wholesale, the main-branch allowlist, protect-branches.sh and the docs-drift checker had no automated coverage anywhere, and a fail-open bug in protect-branches.sh reached main unnoticed — the cleanup DS-145 existed for. `.github/agents/**` and `.claude/**` hold executable governance (hooks, allowlists, skill definitions), now covered inside `npm run ci` by validate:governance-docs and test:governance-hooks. Skipping them re-opens exactly that hole. The cost being optimized away is also gone: a full local run is ~2m24s of local machine time (143-146s across the last five ledger entries), with no runner minutes, queue, or billing attached.

Original ticket text follows for the record. Discovered during DS-140 PR #75: ci.yml's paths-ignore covers .claude/**, .github/memory/**, .github/*.md, docs/**, tracker/** — but .github/*.md only matches files directly in .github/, not subdirectories, so new files under .github/agents/** (e.g. rebase.agent.md) still trigger CI even when the rest of a PR's changes are pure docs/skill/tracker content with no code. Add .github/agents/** to both the push and pull_request paths-ignore lists in ci.yml. Note: pull_request-triggered workflows read the workflow YAML from the base branch (main), not the PR head — so this fix only affects PRs opened after it merges, not any PR already in flight. Renumbered from DS-143 on 2026-08-05 — that id collided with an independently-claimed, further-along in-progress ticket (rm-rf-guard scoping fix) in a concurrent worktree.

title: Tracker governance cleanup — main-branch allowlist gap + ticket data-model audit
notes: Merged in PR #80 (squash, feature/ds-145-violations-log-allowlist -> main). Expanded scope (J-directed) beyond the original one-line fix, to address the root cause after this was the third live recurrence of the same bug class (DS-130, DS-141, DS-145): the main-branch allowlist existed only as independently hand-maintained copies (protect-branches.sh, .husky/pre-commit, CLAUDE.md §8, copilot-instructions.md) with no single source of truth and no drift check — .claude/memory/violations.md being missing from one copy is what surfaced it this time, blocking a routine /pr-merge Gate 5 commit on 2026-08-05. Part A: created .claude/config/main-branch-allowlist.txt as the canonical source; protect-branches.sh and .husky/pre-commit now build their allow-pattern from it at runtime, with an explicit fail-safe (missing/empty file → hard block, never silent allow-all); CLAUDE.md and copilot-instructions.md wrap the mirrored bullet list in <!-- ALLOWLIST:START/END --> markers; new scripts/check-governance-docs.mjs compares the canonical file against both docs as normalized, unordered sets (verified against reordering — passes — and entry removal — fails with a clear diff), wired into .husky/pre-commit as a new conditional Section 6. scripts/protect-main.sh was investigated and found to be live (registered via .github/agents/commit.agent.md, not dead code as first assessed) with an intentionally stricter zero-exception policy correct by design for the Copilot /commit path — left untouched. Part B: found scripts/validate-tracker.mjs's VALID_STATUSES already includes all 7 values (backlog/in-progress/pending-review/committed/done/blocked/removed) but .claude/commands/tracker-update.md and CLAUDE.md's status table each documented a different, incomplete subset — both corrected to the full 7, with tracker-update.md's permission-model paragraph rewritten per J's tracker-is-an-admin-aid clarification (in-progress/pending-review/committed/done move automatically off real events; committed/done stay mechanically gated by tracker-status-guard.sh; backlog/blocked/removed are J-only exception states, never inferred). check-governance-docs.mjs's second check enforces status-enum parity across both docs against validate-tracker.mjs, marker-anchored the same way. Also synced .github/memory/violations.md from .claude/memory/violations.md (208 lines of drift, Rule 15). Two-commit structure on this one ticket/branch/PR: Commit 1 = Part A (allowlist infra), Commit 2 = Part B + this ticket's own notes/tracker regen. Full risk assessment and self-evaluation of mitigations completed before implementation, per J's explicit requirement. Post-implementation self-audit (J declined manual diff review, asked instead whether the solution fully solves the identified problems and whether it introduces anything new) found and closed two remaining gaps before sign-off: (1) copilot-instructions.md's status-enum table was hand-corrected to the right 7 values but had no <!-- STATUS-ENUM:START/END --> markers and was excluded from check-governance-docs.mjs's checkStatusEnum() targets — a third hand-maintained, drift-unchecked copy of the exact disease this ticket exists to cure; fixed by adding markers and adding the file to targets. (2) .husky/pre-commit's allowlist-line parsing only filtered fully-comment/blank lines and did not strip trailing inline '#' comments the way protect-branches.sh does — dormant today (no current entries have inline comments) but would have made the two hook consumers of the same canonical file silently disagree the moment one gained an inline comment; fixed to match protect-branches.sh's strip-then-trim logic exactly, verified via a scratch parity test. Both fixes re-verified: check-governance-docs.mjs passes clean, .husky/pre-commit syntax-checks clean under both bash 3.2 and bash 4+. A second, independent re-validation pass (J-requested, post-sign-off-request) caught one more real regression introduced by the inline-comment fix itself: the fixed .husky/pre-commit read the allowlist via a bare `done < .claude/config/main-branch-allowlist.txt` redirect with no prior existence check, unlike protect-branches.sh's `if [[ -f "$ALLOWLIST_FILE" ]]` guard. Tested directly: under bash 3.2 (the real shebang-invocation binary) a missing file still triggered the fail-safe correctly by accident, but under a newer bash (e.g. if invoked via `bash script.sh` rather than the shebang) `set -e` aborted the script immediately on the failed redirect, before the friendly BLOCKED message could print — a version-dependent, non-deterministic gap. Fixed by adding the same `-f` existence guard protect-branches.sh already had, verified deterministic under both bash binaries × 3 edge cases (missing/empty/comments-only file), and verified both hooks' parsed entry sets are byte-identical against the real production allowlist file. End-to-end gap closed (J-requested): built a disposable scratch git repo (/tmp, deleted after) with a real `main` branch, real husky wiring, and the actual .husky/pre-commit content (only Section 1's unrelated commit-approved flag check stubbed out — never the real /tmp flag) — ran 4 real `git commit` invocations: allowlisted file on main (succeeded), disallowed file on main (blocked with the correct message), allowlist file deliberately removed (fail-safe blocked with the correct message), disallowed file on a non-main branch (succeeded, branch guard correctly scoped to main only). All 4 passed exactly as expected. J then asked directly what happens on the untested 'malformed-but-non-empty allowlist line' edge case and whether it's quickly fixable — tested directly (not reasoned about) via a constructed line containing an unescaped, unbalanced ERE metacharacter (a plausible real typo like a stray '(' in a filename). Confirmed against the real system /usr/bin/grep (BSD grep), not just this tool's ugrep-aliased shell function, that protect-branches.sh's grep -vE-based matching fails OPEN, not closed: an invalid regex makes grep -vE error with empty stdout, which the surrounding `if [[ -n "$DISALLOWED" ]]` check can't distinguish from 'nothing disallowed' — silently allowing a commit/push containing a genuinely disallowed file. This contradicted the original plan's Self-Evaluation table, which had called this residual risk 'Low, theoretical.' .husky/pre-commit's glob-based matching was separately confirmed unaffected (tested directly) since it never compiles a regex. J then explicitly asked not to patch-fix this (i.e. not just escape more ERE metacharacters) and to build a robust solution instead. Root-caused the real issue: protect-branches.sh's design of compiling allowlist-file content into a single combined regex made ANY future malformed line a total, silent bypass for the whole check — a structural single point of failure, not a bug in the specific escaping list. Fix: replaced the regex-alternation + grep -vE approach in protect-branches.sh with the same literal-prefix bash string comparison (`[[ "$FILE" == "$pattern"* ]]`) already used safely by .husky/pre-commit — no regex is ever constructed, so no line's content can fail to compile; both hooks now share one matching mechanism instead of two that could drift. Also quoted the pattern variable in .husky/pre-commit's existing match (previously unquoted, which let bash glob-interpret characters like '?'/'[...]' in a pattern line — a smaller, bounded risk than protect-branches.sh's total-bypass risk, but closed for true parity). Re-verified with 9 distinct malformed-line variants (unbalanced paren, bare asterisk, bracket class, dollar, caret, pipe, backslash, plus+curly, combined garble) — a genuinely disallowed file stayed correctly blocked in every case, proving the whole vulnerability class is closed, not just the one instance found. Re-ran a regression check against the real production allowlist file (no behavior change for legitimate entries) and a fresh disposable end-to-end git-commit test with the actual fixed .husky/pre-commit against a malformed-line allowlist: disallowed file on main still blocked, allowed file on main still succeeded. Both hook files re-verified with bash -n under bash 5.x and /bin/bash 3.2. J then asked what a 1-10 confidence/risk self-assessment looked like for the fix (excluding the canonical-file single-point-of-failure, already accepted by design) — 9/10 confidence, 2/10 residual risk, naming the one honest remaining gap: no CI regression coverage for this logic, since .github/workflows/ci.yml's paths-ignore excludes .claude/** entirely, so a future regression in these files would trigger no automated signal at all. J asked what closing that gap would take, then approved Option B (a new, narrowly-scoped CI workflow rather than editing ci.yml's paths-ignore) and confirmed folding this into DS-145 rather than a new ticket. Wrote scripts/test-governance-hooks.sh: a committed, bash-3.2-compatible regression suite that runs the REAL protect-branches.sh, .husky/pre-commit, and check-governance-docs.mjs (not copies of their logic) against isolated /tmp fixtures — covering missing-allowlist fail-safe, the malformed-line fail-open regression (both hooks), no-regression against the real production allowlist, and docs-drift in both directions (reorder passes, entry/status removal fails with a clear diff). Includes a meta-test that inline-reconstructs the OLD pre-fix regex-based matching logic and confirms it actually does fail open on the same malformed line — proving the suite would have caught DS-145's original bug, not just that it passes against already-fixed code. Chose inline reconstruction over `git show HEAD:...`-based historical diffing deliberately: after this ticket's own commit lands, HEAD becomes the fixed version, which would make a history-based comparison meaningless for all future runs; the inline old-logic snapshot stays a valid comparison point permanently. Iterated twice on fixture bugs during verification (not hook bugs): the STATUS-ENUM fixture used a leading-pipe table-row format that check-governance-docs.mjs's extractPipeTokens() correctly parses as a single-cell table row rather than a flat list, and scenarios F/G were incorrectly staging the allowlist file itself alongside the test file, which is not itself allowlisted and caused an unrelated block — both fixed, full suite now passes 11/11 clean under both bash 3.2 and bash 5.x. Added .github/workflows/governance-hooks.yml: a separate workflow (not an edit to ci.yml) with its own positive paths: allowlist scoped to exactly the 9 relevant files (the two hook scripts, the canonical allowlist, check-governance-docs.mjs, validate-tracker.mjs, the new test script, and the three governed docs), running scripts/test-governance-hooks.sh on push/PR to main — lower-risk than carving exceptions out of ci.yml's ignore list since it never touches the existing build-and-test job's trigger config, and doesn't run the full ~15-minute pipeline on unrelated .claude/ edits. YAML structure validated via Ruby's bundled YAML parser (10 paths under each trigger, 1 job, 3 steps) since neither PyYAML nor js-yaml were available locally.

title: Scope checkbox/radio hover fill per colorScheme instead of global neutral token
notes:
mms-checkbox and mms-radio's `.hover-bg` background uses `background: var(--color-surface-hover)`, which resolves to `var(--color-neutral-3)` identically across all 6 theme files (default/default-dark/maximus/maximus-dark/va-gov/va-gov-dark) — zero variation by colorScheme or brand theme. Verified against Marina (ui-kit) reference: its equivalent tokens (`--global-fill-brand-hover-control` for checkbox/radio-only, `--toggle-oncircle-hover` for toggle) vary per theme block and are frequently brand-tinted (e.g. supplementary-blue-200/300, purple, teal, yellow, green), only falling back to neutral in themes without a distinct brand identity. The token name itself ('...-brand-hover-control') signals brand-awareness was the intended design. mms's flat global neutral is a deviation from Marina that was never flagged/reasoned about per the Phase 1 token workflow (CLAUDE.md ยง4) — it happened because `--color-surface-hover` (defined for table-rows/list-items) was reused for interactive-control hover without checking Marina's separate, brand-aware tokens for these specific controls.

Fix direction (J's proposal, confirmed correct and simpler than inventing a new global structural token): reuse the existing per-component colorScheme custom-property injection already present in both components' `:host([color-scheme='X'])` blocks (where `--_fill` / `--_fill-hover` are defined today, e.g. `--_fill-hover: var(--color-secondary-10, var(--color-secondary-9))`). Add an analogous scoped hover-background custom property (e.g. `--_hover-bg`) in each of those same blocks, mapped to a light step of that scheme's own palette (candidate: `--color-{scheme}-2` — Tier 3 decorative palettes like `accent` define steps 1, 2, 9 so step-2 exists across every tier; no fallback is needed, unlike `--_fill-hover`'s step-10→step-9 fallback). Then change `.hover-bg`'s hover rule in both components from `background: var(--color-surface-hover)` to `background: var(--_hover-bg)`.

Scope: mms-checkbox and mms-radio ONLY. Toggle is explicitly excluded from this ticket per J's direction (2026-08-06) — toggle's colorScheme-scoped hover-bg fix is being done directly in DS-032 (the ticket/worktree already in flight for mms-toggle), not deferred here. This ticket covers checkbox and radio, which need their own worktree/pickup since they weren't already part of an in-progress ticket.

Work needed when picked up: confirm the right light step per scheme (visual check against Marina's actual rendered brand-hover intensity, not just token name matching, and cross-check against the value landed on for toggle in DS-032 so all three stay visually consistent), verify contrast/appearance across all 6 themes x colorSchemes, apply to both components' `.hover-bg` rules (including the size-variant selectors), add/update a11y hover-state test coverage for checkbox.a11y.ts / radio.a11y.ts (currently zero a11y test files exist for either component — separate pre-existing gap tracked under DS-032's audit).

Originally created as DS-145 in this worktree; renumbered to DS-146 after discovering DS-145 was already claimed (in-progress, uncommitted) by a concurrent worktree (feature/ds-145-violations-log-allowlist) that my origin/main-only fetch didn't catch.

Scope expanded 2026-08-06 (J's direction): checkbox-group and radio-group were originally listed in DS-032's governing plan as in-scope for that ticket's a11y-coverage-taxonomy retrofit, but J pulled all checkbox/radio-related work out of DS-032 entirely — this ticket now also owns applying DS-032's mechanical a11y coverage taxonomy (.claude/contracts/a11y-coverage.md + scripts/audit-a11y-coverage.mjs's COMPONENTS registry) to mms-checkbox, mms-checkbox-group, mms-radio, and mms-radio-group, not just the hover-fill token fix above.

That retrofit diff is NOT preserved as a file anywhere — only the pre-retrofit committed version remains in tests/radio-group.a11y.ts today. Recoverable only by re-deriving it from scratch against the taxonomy, or from the DS-032 session transcript if that's still needed — flag to J before assuming a from-scratch rebuild is fine.

Scope addition 2026-08-10 (surfaced during DS-147's live-table wiring pass): Button, AlertBanner, Toggle, Link, TextField, Modal, Select, and TextArea Overview stories all now read their "WCAG 2.2 AA Compliance" table live from src/generated/wcag-coverage.ts via renderWcagComplianceTable(wcagTables['<key>'].rows) instead of a static hand-authored table — see DS-147. Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Radio, and RadioGroup are the only remaining components still on static tables, and only because wcag-coverage.ts has zero audit data for them (a direct consequence of the a11y-test-file gap this ticket already owns). Once this ticket lands audit coverage for all four (checkbox.a11y.ts, checkbox-group.a11y.ts, radio.a11y.ts, radio-group.a11y.ts) and regenerates wcag-coverage.ts via `npm run build-wcag-tables`, wiring their four Overview stories to renderWcagComplianceTable is part of THIS ticket's completion — not a separate follow-up ticket. Mirror the exact pattern already applied to the eight components above.

Unrelated infra bug folded in at J's direction 2026-08-11 (not DS-146 scope, tracked here per J's explicit instruction rather than a new ticket): `.claude/hooks/pr-create-guard.sh` (and identically, `pr-merge-guard.sh`) write their BLOCKED message to stdout, but the harness reads stderr for PreToolUse hook block reasons. The hook parses `tool_input.command` via a python3 one-liner, checks if it matches `gh pr create` (regex anchored to start/`&&`/`||`/`;`), and if `/tmp/pr-create-approved` doesn't exist, does:

echo "BLOCKED: Cannot create a PR without J's scope approval."
echo "The /pr-create skill creates /tmp/pr-create-approved in Gate 3 — J's approval in Gate 1 is what authorizes that."
exit 2

Both `echo` calls go to stdout, not stderr. When Claude Code surfaces a PreToolUse hook's non-zero exit to the model, it reads stderr for the reason — so instead of the intended `BLOCKED: ...` message, the model sees a generic `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: [.claude/hooks/pr-create-guard.sh]: No stderr output`, with the real reason silently swallowed.

Trigger scenario: sending `touch /tmp/pr-create-approved && gh pr create ...` as one compound Bash call. The hook evaluates the whole command string before any of it executes, so the flag doesn't exist yet at check time — the hook correctly detects "not approved," but the block message never reaches the model because of the stdout/stderr bug. Looked like a mystery failure until splitting `touch` and `gh pr create` into two separate Bash calls (matching what the skill file already shows as two separate bash blocks) resolved it.

Fix: redirect both `echo` lines (and the equivalent two lines in `pr-merge-guard.sh`) to stderr, e.g. `echo "BLOCKED: ..." >&2`. That alone would have made the real failure reason visible on the first attempt instead of the opaque generic error.

Secondary, separate observation (not a hook bug, but worth knowing): even after correctly splitting into two calls, a standalone `touch /tmp/pr-create-approved` got denied twice by the Auto Mode permission classifier as a suspected gate-bypass pattern — it only went through after J gave direct in-chat "Yes" authorization. Not something to fix in the hook script, just a heads-up in case the same thing happens again.

Merged in PR #93. Merged with the required "Build & Test" CI check in a FAIL state, per J's explicit override (2026-08-11) under time pressure — this was NOT a real test regression: the a11y step ran the full unscoped 517-test suite serially (`workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined` in playwright.config.ts, despite `fullyParallel: true`) and was still ~93% complete (480/517) when the job hit its 15m0s hard timeout and was canceled. Fix identified but NOT yet actioned — needs a separate follow-up ticket to bump `workers` to ~4 in CI (estimated ~3-4 min full-suite runtime) and/or raise the job timeout in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

title: mms-button primary variant fails WCAG 1.4.3 text contrast in dark mode
notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-06 while building tests/button.a11y.ts's Dark mode block under DS-032 — the FIRST-EVER dark-mode a11y coverage for mms-button. --color-text-on-primary (#ffffff, identical value in both src/themes/maximus.css and maximus-dark.css) rendered against --color-primary-9 in src/themes/maximus-dark.css (#876ad2) measures 4.18:1 — below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal-size text (WCAG 1.4.3). Confirmed via a live axe scan against the running Storybook instance (port 6032), not just static token math.

This is a brand token-sheet defect, not a mms-button component bug: mms-button.component.ts sets --_solid: var(--color-primary-9) and --_on-solid: var(--color-text-on-primary) for the primary variant and renders them correctly per the token contract; the dark theme's chosen primary-9 shade is what fails CLAUDE.md §3.3's explicit rule ("color.text.on-primary must satisfy 4.5:1 contrast against color.brand.primary"). Blast radius is every component that uses --color-primary-9 as a solid dark-mode fill with white text on top, not just button — worth checking for other consumers once picked up.

Related, surfaced in the same investigation: scripts/contrast-audit.mjs (296/296 passing, wired into CI) hardcodes only ONE color table per theme name as JS literals in its own source rather than reading live CSS — its maximus.primary[9] value is #502E91, which is maximus.css's LIGHT-theme value. There is no dark-mode table anywhere in the script for any theme, so it structurally could not have caught this regression and cannot catch future dark-mode-only token regressions either. Whether to extend the script to cover dark-mode palettes (needs real dark values for va-gov-dark/default-dark too, not just maximus-dark) or treat it as an explicitly light-mode-only sanity check is a decision for whoever picks this up.

title: Allowlist skill-driven approval-flag touches so auto-mode classifier stops blocking /commit, /pr-create, /pr-merge
notes: Root cause: .claude/settings.json permissions.allow lists every other shell verb (rm, mv, cp, chmod, etc.) with wildcard allow rules, but `touch` was never added. Any `touch /tmp/*-approved` therefore falls through to the Claude Code auto-mode classifier for a judgment call, and the classifier pattern-matches Kai touching a known approval-flag path as circumvention -- with no visibility into whether it's mid-execution of a skill (/commit, /pr-create, /pr-merge) the user already invoked and approved. This blocked /pr-create twice live during DS-032's PR #81 creation, requiring J to intervene mid-workflow -- exactly the friction the 15-rule governance model was built to eliminate. Fix: add three narrowly-scoped exact-match allow entries -- Bash(touch /tmp/commit-approved), Bash(touch /tmp/pr-create-approved), Bash(touch /tmp/pr-merge-approved) -- to .claude/settings.json's permissions.allow array. Deliberately excludes /tmp/force-push-approved and /tmp/rm-rf-approved, which CLAUDE.md reserves for J to create manually -- those should stay outside Kai's allowlist. Verification: after the change, re-run a live /commit or /pr-create-style touch of one of these three flags and confirm no classifier denial occurs. Merged via PR #82 on 2026-08-08.

title: expectResponsiveReflowCompliance leaves the Playwright viewport resized — no reset after the 320px Reflow check
notes:
Found 2026-08-09/10 while fixing mms-alert-banner's real Reflow defect (DS-018). tests/a11y-utils.ts's expectNoHorizontalScrollAtReflow (WCAG 1.4.10) calls page.setViewportSize({width: 320, height: 256}) but never restores the original viewport afterward. expectResponsiveReflowCompliance then runs expectNoContentLossAtZoom (1.4.4) and expectNoClippingWithTextSpacing (1.4.12) in sequence on the same page — both execute at the leftover 320px viewport rather than a clean/default one, even though only the first check's own SC is actually about viewport width. Contrast with expectNoContentLossAtZoom, which does correctly reset document.body.style.zoom back to '1' after itself. Shared test infrastructure (tests/a11y-utils.ts) — affects every component whose .a11y.ts file calls expectResponsiveReflowCompliance (toggle, modal, link, select, text-field, text-area per DS-032 Part 5, plus alert-banner as of DS-018), not just alert-banner. Out of scope for DS-018's alert-banner-only worktree; needs its own ticket. Fix should restore the pre-call viewport size (or a documented default) at the end of expectNoHorizontalScrollAtReflow, or explicitly at the end of the expectResponsiveReflowCompliance umbrella, so 1.4.4/1.4.12 checks and any assertions a caller makes afterward aren't silently run at a shrunk viewport.

RESOLVED 2026-08-10: expectNoHorizontalScrollAtReflow now captures page.viewportSize() before resizing and restores it in a finally block, so restoration happens even if the assertion itself fails. Restore failures are caught and logged via console.warn rather than thrown, so a broken cleanup can never mask the real Reflow assertion result. Verified via the full unscoped npm run test:a11y suite (270 tests across all 7 components) — 0 failures. A related, narrower, purely theoretical gap in expectNoContentLossAtZoom (zoom reset skipped only if its own clip-check throws — not observed in any current test) was spun out separately as DS-154, phase post-mvp1.

Merged in PR #86.

title: Fix specPasses() to recognize Playwright flaky-but-recovered tests as passing
notes: Surfaced during DS-018/PR #84 CI investigation (2026-08-10). scripts/audit-a11y-coverage.mjs's specPasses() requires every retry-attempt status to be 'passed', so a Playwright test that fails once (e.g. an axe-core re-entrancy race: 'Error: Axe is already running...') and then passes on retry is reported by Playwright as an overall pass ('flaky') but is NOT recognized as a pass by specPasses(). Since the status never hits 'skipped' either, fixmeReason() also returns undefined, producing an uncited, blank-description FAIL row in the generated WCAG table instead of a clean PASS or a cited pre-existing finding. Confirmed via PR #84: alert-banner's a11y test failed CI on first run due to this exact scenario, then passed clean (29 PASS/0 FAIL) on CI re-run with identical code. Fixed: flattenSuites() now reads each test's own outcome status (t.status: 'expected'|'unexpected'|'flaky'|'skipped') instead of flattening per-retry-attempt statuses from results[]. specPasses() now accepts 'expected' or 'flaky' as passing. Verified: synthetically reproduced the exact PR #84 scenario (patched the alert-banner 'has no a11y violations' test to fail-then-pass with the real axe re-entrancy error message) — confirmed it produced the same 2 uncited FAIL rows on the pre-fix code, and resolved cleanly to 29 PASS/0 FAIL with the fix applied. 593/593 unit tests still pass; no other code references the changed statuses shape. Risk identified on review (2026-08-10): treating all 'flaky' as passing uniformly could silently mask a genuine intermittent component defect that also happens to clear within CI's 2-retry budget, not just known CI-infra flakiness — the fix as originally shipped had no way to distinguish the two. Mitigated per J's accepted recommendation: added a non-blocking '⚠ FLAKY' annotation. hasFlaky(entry) checks entry.statuses.includes('flaky'); resultRow() now carries an optional flaky field; all 5 call sites where specPasses() produces a PASS/FAIL row (ARIA/Keyboard, Responsive/Reflow, Timing & Motion, Color/Contrast, Target Size/Touch Area) pass through whether the underlying entry/entries included a 'flaky' outcome. main() prints a '⚠ FLAKY [state] category — passed on retry, review before trusting as stable' line per flagged row and a '(N FLAKY, non-blocking)' suffix on the Total line — purely additive, does not affect specPasses()'s PASS/FAIL determination, the PASS/FAIL/N/A tallies, or the exit code (totalFail > 0 || totalBuildGap > 0). Re-verified with the same synthetic-flaky-reproduction method: patched alert-banner's a11y test to the exact fail-then-pass PR #84 scenario — confirmed the FLAKY annotation appears ('⚠ FLAKY [default] Keyboard/Operability'), PASS count stays 29, exit code stays 0. 593/593 unit tests still pass. Follow-up review (2026-08-10): J asked to evaluate risk in the FLAKY mitigation itself. Found the annotation only reached raw CLI stdout — it did not propagate into either human-facing artifact built for this exact kind of review (each component's WCAG compliance table, the Live Coverage Grid), and manualRow() (the ARIA icon-naming carve-out) silently dropped flaky entirely, both bucket-scoped (flakyPasses) and all-rows CLI tallies. J selected 'fix now, same ticket'. Fixed: summarizeCategory() now returns {result, reason, flaky} (flaky = true if any row of the winning outcome was flaky — FAIL/BUILD GAP/MANUAL/PAGE-LEVEL/PASS priority unchanged); manualRow() gained a flaky param and its one call site (ARIA icon-naming) now passes scoped.some(hasFlaky); main()'s CLI tally renamed flakyPasses -> flakyRows, scanning ALL rows (not just PASS-bucket) so the MANUAL carve-out's flaky signal isn't dropped from the CLI summary either. scripts/build-wcag-tables.mjs's buildComponentTable() now destructures flaky from both summarizeCategory() call sites (per-component table + Live Coverage Grid cells); implementationText() appends a '(⚠ recovered from a flaky run — confirm this isn't a genuine intermittent defect before trusting as stable)' caveat to PASS rows; GridCell interface gained flaky?: boolean. src/stories/foundations/Accessibility.stories.ts's summaryBadge() now appends '(⚠ N FLAKY)' to the Live Coverage Grid's per-component summary; componentGridTable() cells add a ⚠ marker + title tooltip. Added regression coverage: src/stories/foundations/Accessibility.flaky.test.ts (5 tests) pins summarizeCategory()'s flaky-propagation behavior directly — single flaky PASS row, flaky among mixed PASS rows, no-flaky baseline, flaky MANUAL row (the manualRow gap), and confirms flaky doesn't leak from a losing PASS row into a winning FAIL outcome. Re-ran the full test:a11y suite (`npx playwright test`, all 7 components, 263 passed/7 skipped, 0 flaky) to regenerate src/generated/wcag-coverage.ts with complete data — diff showed only 2 result changes, both alert-banner (Responsive/Reflow, Target Size/Touch Area: FAIL -> PASS), a pre-existing staleness in the PR #84/DS-018 commit itself (that PR's own defect-fix was never followed by a regeneration before merge) unrelated to this ticket's changes; confirmed via a clean isolated run of tests/alert-banner.a11y.ts (36/36 passed). Re-ran the synthetic-flaky-reproduction method end-to-end through the full pipeline this time (not just CLI): confirmed GridCell.flaky=true on both the affected Semantic/ARIA (MANUAL) and Keyboard/Operability (PASS) cells, and the WCAG table's implementation text carries the recovered-from-flaky caveat — then reverted the synthetic patch and regenerated wcag-coverage.ts back to its real clean state (0 flaky, since nothing is genuinely flaky right now). 598/598 unit tests pass (593 + 5 new). Follow-up UI polish on the Live Coverage Grid (2026-08-10, J live review): (1) sorted components alphabetically in LiveCoverageGrid's render (not the canonical COMPONENTS array, which other tooling depends on); (2) diagnosed the reported 'page wiggles' as the native <details> sibling-cascade effect (measured 314px shift) — inherent to stacking multiple <details>, not fixed by the alphabetical sort (flagged to J that sorting relocates which component is wiggle-exempt, doesn't remove the wiggle); (3) fixed a real CSF bug — CATEGORY_STATE_APPLICABILITY (a plain data export used by Accessibility.applicability.test.ts) was being auto-discovered by Storybook as a bogus, non-rendering sidebar story; excluded via excludeStories on the default export; (4) fixed table header font size (0.875rem -> 0.75rem) and, after J found the table overflowing its container on expand, added table-layout: fixed + a narrow State column width, plus a display-only formatCategoryLabel() that inserts a breakable space around '/' (e.g. 'Color/Contrast' -> 'Color / Contrast') so long headers wrap to a second line instead of forcing the table wider than its container. Verified live via mcp__playwright__* against the running Storybook dev server (port 6100): table width 926px within a 960px container, headers wrap at the intended break points, bogus sidebar entry gone. All within src/stories/foundations/Accessibility.stories.ts, same file already in this ticket's diff. Merged in PR #87.

title: Decouple audit:a11y-coverage exit code from already-cited/tracked findings
notes: Surfaced during PR #81's /pr-merge: CI's Build & Test check failed at the audit:a11y-coverage step on 7 FAIL (mms-modal, all test.fixme()'d citing DS-148) and 5 BUILD GAP (mms-text-area, citing DS-149) rows -- both pre-existing, already-tracked findings, but the script's current exit-code policy blocks on any FAIL/BUILD GAP regardless of citation status. J assessed this as CI overreach ("exists to ensure the build comes through, not as a police to check for a11y") and directed merging anyway; no branch protection currently enforces this check, so it didn't block the merge, but it should stop producing false-alarm CI failures for findings that are already tracked and cited. Fix: audit-a11y-coverage.mjs's exit-code logic should only return non-zero for FAIL/BUILD GAP rows that lack a fixme/citation reason pointing to an existing tracker ticket -- rows with a cited reason (e.g. "see DS-148") should not block CI, since they represent known, tracked debt rather than a regression. Genuinely uncited/new FAIL or BUILD GAP rows must still fail the build. Committed 88e0c55 on feature/ds-153-audit-exit-code-scoping -- verified build-wcag-tables.mjs/Live Coverage Grid unaffected (summarizeCategory/GridCell never reference cited). Merged in PR #88.

title: expectNoContentLossAtZoom skips zoom reset if the clip-check itself throws
notes: Found 2026-08-10 during DS-151's adversarial self-review of the viewport-reset fix in tests/a11y-utils.ts. expectNoContentLossAtZoom (WCAG 1.4.4) resets document.body.style.zoom back to '1' on the line immediately before its expect() assertion -- but that reset only runs if the preceding page.locator(containerSelector).evaluate(...) clip-check itself resolves. If that call throws (selector never attaches / times out, or the page/context closes), the zoom reset is skipped entirely, same class of leftover-state bug DS-151 fixed for the viewport. Purely theoretical today: every current caller (toggle, modal, link, select, text-field, text-area, alert-banner) already page.waitForSelector()s the same container before calling expectResponsiveReflowCompliance, so the locator is guaranteed present by construction -- confirmed via the full 270-test a11y suite passing clean with 0 occurrences. Only becomes live if a future component's Reflow test passes a containerSelector for something legitimately transient (async-loaded or conditionally-rendered). Fix (when picked up): wrap the clip-check in try/finally the same way expectNoHorizontalScrollAtReflow now does, so the zoom reset is unconditional.

title: Streamline a11y summary & reporting — surface MANUAL-review WCAG rows prominently
notes: Surfaced during DS-147 live verification (2026-08-10) — J asked whether WCAG rows with a MANUAL result (currently just a gray chip in a 12+ row table, easy to scroll past) should get more prominent visual treatment at the component level, universally across all components rather than per-component. Implemented as manualReviewCallout(rows) in src/stories/shared/a11y-outcome.ts, called automatically at the top of renderWcagComplianceTable — a single shared-renderer change so every component's Overview page picks it up with no per-story edits. Currently alert-banner is the only component with MANUAL rows (SC 1.3.1 and 4.1.2, both icon-name meaningfulness requiring human review) — live-verified via Playwright: callout renders above the table, table itself unaffected, 0 console errors. Kept as its own ticket separate from the Toggle/Link/TextField/Button live-table wiring (folded into DS-147 itself) given the different mechanical risk profile: this touches a file shared by every component's Overview page that reads from it (Button, AlertBanner, Toggle, Link, TextField), not just a handful of components — a regression here has multi-component blast radius. Re-verified Button (a pre-existing renderWcagComplianceTable consumer not touched this session) still renders correctly post-change via Playwright — 0 regressions, table intact, no stray callout (zero MANUAL rows, correct). Correction while re-verifying: Select.stories.ts is NOT actually a renderWcagComplianceTable consumer — it still has its own static, hand-authored 3-column WCAG table (no Result column, no outcome chips), unrelated to this change and unaffected by it. The only current consumers of the shared renderer are Button, AlertBanner, Toggle, Link, and TextField.
flag_for_future_ticket: Select.stories.ts's WCAG table is still static/hand-authored (same gap DS-147/DS-155-wiring fixed elsewhere) — candidate for a future DS ticket, not addressed here. UPDATE 2026-08-10: superseded — Select was wired to renderWcagComplianceTable under DS-147's all-components wiring pass, so this no longer applies.
notes_addendum_2026_08_10:
Second shared-renderer change under this ticket: J flagged that a viewer landing on any component's Overview page might read a WCAG table listing e.g. 10 SCs and wonder why dozens of other WCAG 2.2 AA criteria aren't shown — the table could read as an incomplete audit rather than an intentionally-scoped one. Added a footnote paragraph directly below the table in renderWcagComplianceTable (src/stories/shared/a11y-outcome.ts), below the manualReviewCallout addition from earlier in this ticket: "Only Success Criteria applicable to this component's role and content type are listed above — omitted SCs were evaluated and found not applicable, not overlooked." Same shared-file blast radius as the MANUAL callout, so kept in this ticket rather than opened separately. Live-verified via Playwright across three representative consumers — Button (baseline), AlertBanner (confirms the footnote coexists cleanly with the MANUAL callout above it), and TextArea (confirms it renders correctly alongside BUILD GAP rows too) — 0 console errors on all three, footnote text present and correctly positioned in each. Follow-up same day: J flagged the footnote's original treatment (0.75rem font, opacity: 0.65 on a `

`) as failing an accessible-font-size bar — undercutting a note whose entire point is legibility of scope. Replaced with a bordered callout (`applicabilityNote()`), same visual pattern as `manualReviewCallout` — solid `color` (no opacity), 0.8125rem font, background/border-left using the existing `OUTCOME_COLORS['N/A']` blue pairing (distinct from MANUAL's neutral gray, since this is informational rather than an action item). Re-verified via Playwright on the same three consumers (Button, AlertBanner, TextArea) — 0 console errors, callout renders as a div (not a low-opacity paragraph) below the table in all three, coexists correctly with both the MANUAL callout and BUILD GAP rows. Open design question raised in the same discussion, not yet resolved: whether to keep the callout+footnote approach at all, versus showing the full fixed 18-SC catalog (CATEGORY_WCAG_MAP's 7 categories) per component with explicit N/A rows for inapplicable SCs instead of omitting them. Current buildComponentTable() in scripts/build-wcag-tables.mjs already computes the N/A determination at the category level and then discards it (`if (result === 'N/A') continue`) before it reaches wcagTables — surfacing it instead would be a small, bounded change (max ~8 extra rows per component) given the fixed 18-SC universe, not the open-ended lift originally assumed. Not implemented — exploratory, pending J's direction on which approach to keep. Merged in PR #89.

title: Build mms-multi-select (Marina: Select Multiple)
notes: All 5 test layers pass. a11y-test surfaced a real aria-required-children defect (search-container was a non-option direct child of role=listbox) — J approved fix, moved role=listbox onto a new inner .listbox wrapper separate from search-container. DS-149 autocomplete gap carried forward as cited BUILD GAP (non-blocking). Post-handoff refactor: J asked whether the option-row checkbox glyph reused mms-checkbox — it did not (couldn't: nested native input inside role=option breaks the listbox's single-tab-stop model). Extracted the shared visual (box/glyph/paint) into src/components/checkbox/checkbox-indicator.parts.ts, keyed by data-size/data-state instead of :host(...) so it's portable; refactored mms-checkbox (already merged, PR #93) to consume it and wired it into multi-select's decorative aria-hidden option glyph. Unifying on the shared partial also corrected a 1px checkmark-position discrepancy multi-select's old hand-rolled version had (top: 1px -> top: 0px, matching mms-checkbox's canonical md value). Re-ran all 5 layers for both components post-refactor: unit 66/66 (checkbox) + 68/68 (multi-select), full a11y suite 726 passed/3 skipped/0 failed, coverage audit checkbox 51 PASS/0 FAIL + multi-select 30 PASS/0 FAIL (same 5 cited DS-149 BUILD GAP rows, unrelated), token validation 50/50, hardcoded clean, Storybook build succeeded. Second post-handoff fix: J flagged that mms-multi-select carried a Marina-only `variant` prop ('gray-fill'/'white-black-fill'/'minimal') never cross-checked against established mms form-field conventions — neither mms-select nor mms-text-field has any variant/fill prop, both use a single transparent/bordered container styled purely by state. Per J's explicit decision, dropped MultiSelectVariant entirely: removed the type, the @property, and ~90 lines of variant-gated CSS, consolidating to a single-treatment container matching mms-select's pattern (state-driven only: filled/hover/focus/open/error/disabled/readonly). Removed all downstream references — test file (68->66 tests, dropped variant-default and accepts-all-variants tests), Storybook Variants demo section + argTypes + snippet-builder + render args, and the MultiSelectVariant barrel export in src/index.ts. Re-ran full re-verification: typecheck clean, unit 66/66, token validation 49/49, hardcoded clean, full a11y suite 726 passed/3 skipped/0 failed, coverage audit 30 PASS/0 FAIL/28 N/A/5 BUILD GAP (same cited DS-149 gap, unrelated) exit 0, WCAG tables regenerated exit 0, Storybook production build exit 0. Zero regressions from the variant removal. Third post-handoff fix: J flagged the size prop as half-baked — label-row font wasn't scaling from sm to md to lg, pointing to mms-text-field's convention as the reference. Confirmed via source read: both mms-select and mms-text-field scale .label-row font-size/line-height via :host([size='sm'/'lg']) overrides; multi-select's .label-row was hardcoded to --type-ui-label-md-size/-weight with no size-scoped overrides at all. Fixed by adding letter-spacing to the base rule and :host([size='sm']) / :host([size='lg']) .label-row overrides using the matching --type-ui-label-sm/lg-size/-line-height/-letter-spacing tokens (full ui-label ladder already exists in tokens-semantic.css; weight is constant across the ladder so left unscoped). Also caught and fixed a second, related gap while comparing against mms-select: .dropdown-icon's right-offset was fixed at --spacing-sm2 regardless of size, while mms-select scales it (--spacing-sm1 at sm, --spacing-md1 at lg) to stay aligned with the size-scaled padding — added matching overrides. Re-ran full re-verification: typecheck clean (same 8 pre-existing unrelated errors only), unit 66/66, token validation 57 refs PASS, hardcoded clean, full a11y suite 726 passed/3 skipped/0 failed, coverage audit 30 PASS/0 FAIL/28 N/A/5 BUILD GAP (same cited DS-149 gap) exit 0, WCAG tables regenerated exit 0, Storybook production build exit 0. Zero regressions. Fourth post-handoff round: J flagged the Playground default (4 programOptions) forcing an internal scroll on Storybook's docs Canvas — root cause was Storybook's `.docs-story` container measuring height once at initial (closed) mount; fixed via `min-height: 300px` on the Playground decorator's outer wrapper so the initial measurement already reserves room for the open state. J also asked for `helperText: ''` as the Playground default (component already conditionally omits the row when falsy, no component change needed). J then flagged that when 'select all' is enabled and a user searches, 'select all' shouldn't remain an option — added a `showSelectAllRow` getter (`showSelectAll && !searchQuery.trim()`) gating both the select-all row and its divider, and fixed a keyboard arrow-nav side effect (`.option-item` query now filters out `hidden` rows). Finally J asked whether the open panel could layer on top of the helper/error text instead of pushing it down — root cause: `.dropdown-panel` (`position: absolute; top: 100%`) was a sibling of `.select-container`, not a child, so it resolved against `:host`'s full flex-column height (trigger + helper/error text) rather than just the trigger box. Fixed by wrapping `.select-container` and `.dropdown-panel` together in a new `.select-wrapper` (`position: relative`) so the panel now overlays the helper/error text, matching the native-`<select>`-style pattern `mms-select` already uses. Re-ran full /test-component: unit 66/66 (no new coverage added for the new showSelectAllRow behavior — worth a follow-up test), full a11y suite 37/37 passed for multi-select (no violations from either the search/select-all change or the panel-overlay CSS restructure), coverage audit 30 PASS/0 FAIL/28 N/A/5 BUILD GAP (same cited DS-149 gap, unrelated) exit 0, WCAG tables regenerated exit 0, token validation 48/48, hardcoded clean, Storybook production build exit 0. Zero regressions. Merged in PR #115.

title: Refactor mms-breadcrumbs to consume ui-label tokens instead of body tokens
notes:
Companion to DS-142 (mms-button) — same root cause, split out because DS-142 already covers a lot for mms-button. Discovered during DS-060 (mms-tabs): the ui-label type scale (--type-ui-label-{sm,md,lg}-size) is being realigned to alias body's size cadence (14/16/18px) while keeping its own weight (500, vs body's 400) and letter-spacing (0.01em) as the deliberate UI-chrome differentiator. mms-breadcrumbs currently uses --type-body-{sm,md}-size directly for all crumbs, with only the current-page crumb getting a hardcoded font-weight:700 override -- non-current (clickable) crumbs fall back to implicit regular weight. Swap breadcrumbs to the corrected --type-ui-label-{sm,md}-size tokens so clickable crumbs render at medium (500) weight, distinct from both body copy and the bolder current-page marker. Breadcrumbs never renders inline within body prose (unlike mms-link, which was deliberately left on body tokens for that reason -- see DS-060 session notes), so this is a clean swap with no inline-text mismatch risk. Scope: font-size/line-height/letter-spacing/weight token swap only, no layout/behavior change. Re-run breadcrumbs a11y suite and visual regression baseline after the swap.

Implementation: mms-breadcrumbs' own CSS can't reach the ui-label tokens into its composed <mms-link> crumbs (shadow DOM encapsulation), so mms-link gained a new opt-in `type-scale` prop/attribute ('body' default | 'ui-label') -- internal-use only, not exposed in the Link story's Controls, documented in its JSDoc as reserved for a composing parent. Swapping ui-label's line-height (1.4 vs body's 1.5) dropped the composed link's clickable box to 22.4px, breaching the WCAG 2.5.8 24px target-size floor (mms-link's default body/md scale sat at exactly 24px with zero margin). Fixed by adding `padding-block: var(--spacing-xs1)` (2px) to the ui-label variant's `.link` rule (not `:host` -- host padding doesn't grow the child .link box that the test actually measures), restoring ~26.4px. Scoped to the opt-in variant only; mms-link's default body behavior is unchanged. Re-ran breadcrumbs + link a11y suites clean (target-size passing, only pre-existing unrelated axe-core concurrency flakes observed, self-resolved on retry). Visual regression baseline: no automated visual-regression tool exists in this repo (no *.visual.ts, no Chromatic/Percy) -- did the manual Storybook check per the testing contract's Layer 5 (sm/md, light/dark) via Playwright screenshot; renders correctly, no layout shift. Merged in PR #9.

A new private _renderStepsDrawer() renders an mms-drawer (size=sm, title-text=this.label, secondary-label='Close', no primary button) whose slotted body is a nested <mms-stepper type="vertical" .items=${this.items}> -- full icon/substep/state fidelity, not an invented summary.
