title: Make Developer Guide/Installation cross-platform (Mac + Windows)
notes:
Raised by a PC-based consumer dev who could not run the Installation guide's opening commands in cmd.exe / VS Code terminal.

Audit of src/stories/developer-guide/02-Installation.stories.ts found three shell-dependent lines:
1. Line 33 `grep "@mms" ~/.npmrc` — no `grep` in PowerShell (it's Select-String) or cmd.exe; `~` does not expand in cmd.exe. Works in Git Bash.
2. Line 36 `sed -i '' '/@mms/d' ~/.npmrc` — BSD sed syntax, macOS-only. No `sed` in PowerShell/cmd.exe, AND GNU sed (Git Bash, WSL, Linux) rejects `-i ''` by reading '' as the script. Fails on every non-macOS shell including the one PC shell that has sed.
3. Line 58 `npm install @mms/design-system \` — backslash line continuation is bash/zsh only. PowerShell uses backtick, cmd.exe uses caret.

Steps 2, 3, 4 and Verify are already platform-neutral.

## Severity reframe — the backslash is the only hard blocker

The grep/sed prereq is CONDITIONAL cleanup (a clean machine doesn't need it). The backslash is in the MANDATORY path. If a PC dev pastes the two-line Step 1 block, the shell splits it into two commands: line 1 runs without `--registry` (it never reaches npm), line 2 runs standalone and errors as an unrecognized command.

Verified live from a clean context (HOME=/tmp/kai-clean-home, isolating both ~/.npmrc and the npm cache):
```
npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@mms%2fdesign-system
npm error 404  The requested resource '@mms/design-system@*' could not be found
              or you do not have permission to access it.
```
The failure is misleading, not loud. "not found or you do not have permission" reads as an unpublished package or broken Artifactory access — nothing points at a backslash. Likely sends devs to escalate to DevOps about permissions, a dead end.

## KEY FINDING — `--registry` cannot override a stale `@mms:registry`

Scoped registry config in .npmrc takes precedence over the `--registry` CLI flag. Verified live:
```
.npmrc:  @mms:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
command: npm view @mms/design-system --registry=https://bogus-host-kai-test.invalid/
result:  GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@mms%2fdesign-system   <- flag ignored entirely
```
This undermines the guide's original design. Per docs/ds-121-investigation-2026-07-21.md the `--registry` flag was chosen specifically to bypass .npmrc after a consumer 401 incident — but it provides ZERO protection against the exact failure mode it was picked to defend against (stale @mms scope config). That is why the grep/sed prereq had to exist at all: a crutch compensating for a flag that cannot do the job.

Corollary: `npm config set @mms:registry=<url>` is strictly better — it writes the key that actually wins precedence, overwriting stale config rather than being silently defeated by it.

## Approach (decided with J)

Do NOT add a parallel Windows tab. A single universal guide, because everything from Step 2 onward is already platform-neutral.

Primary path: project-level `.npmrc` committed to the consuming repo root with the `@mms:registry` line — teammates and CI then run plain `npm install` with zero per-machine setup, and lockfile `resolved` URLs stay consistent so `npm ci` works in the build pipeline. Fallback: per-machine `npm config set @mms:registry=<url>`.

Replace the grep/sed text-munging with npm's own config CLI (`npm config get userconfig` / `get @mms:registry` / `delete @mms:registry` / `delete <host>:_authToken` / `delete <host>:_auth`), byte-identical across macOS zsh, PowerShell, cmd.exe and Git Bash. Verified locally: `get` returns "undefined" when unset, `delete` on an absent key is a silent no-op with exit 0, so a clean machine sees no errors. Also removes the ~/.npmrc path assumption — `npm config get userconfig` prints the real path on any OS. Collapse the Step 1 install to a single line (drop the backslash).

## CORRECTION — barrel import is broken; /standalone IS needed

An earlier note in this ticket claimed tree-shaking was fine and needed no change. That was wrong, and is retracted here.

Measured with esbuild 0.28.1 against the built dist:
```
BARREL  import '@mms/design-system'                  defines: 0   size: 0 bytes
SINGLE  import '.../components/mms-button.component' defines: 2   size: 1,280,272 bytes
```
dist/index.js is 68 real lines with 24 export statements and bundles to ZERO bytes.

Root cause: package.json `sideEffects` lists `**/*.component.js` but NOT `index.js`. The bundler therefore treats the barrel as side-effect-free, drops the entire module, and never walks through to the component files where the sideEffects marking would have applied. The marking never gets a chance to take effect. This is the same failure Marina documents in its README (barrel "tree-shaken to nothing because index files are pure re-exports").

Nuance for the docs: the barrel DOES work without a bundler — a raw <script type="module"> performs no tree-shaking. So 03-HTMLUsage.stories.ts:206 is correct as written. The barrel only vanishes under Vite/Webpack/Rollup.

Per-component subpath imports (03-HTMLUsage.stories.ts:43, 04-ReactUsage.stories.ts:157) work correctly and remain the recommended production path.

## /standalone build — folded into this ticket per J

No technical blockers:
- esbuild 0.28.1 already present in node_modules; promote to a direct devDependency
- ~10 lines added to scripts/build-package.mjs, one esbuild call producing dist/standalone.js with Lit inlined
- Add `./standalone` to package.json exports MANUALLY — verified safe: generate-exports.mjs:72-75 only deletes/regenerates keys starting with `./components/mms-`, so a manual entry survives regeneration
- npm run verify-bundle already exists for validation

Costs (not blockers):
1. Changes the published package — this stops being a docs-only PR. Full CI runs; post-commit code lock applies.
2. Cannot be validated end-to-end without Maximus VPN. Bundle build and shake behavior are verifiable locally; a real consumer install is not.
3. Size: the single-component bundle measured 1.28MB with Lit inlined. Standalone will be larger. Check deliberately before shipping.

Consequence: DS-163 is no longer a pure `ops` ticket — it now carries a build change. Keep the build work in a SEPARATE COMMIT from the docs work so each is reviewable independently.

## Two accuracy fixes found in the same file, unrelated to platform
- Line 198 'Expected output' shows @mms/design-system@0.9.0; current version is 0.21.0.
- Line 61 Yarn note: `--registry=` is Yarn 1 only. Yarn Berry (v2+) ignores it and needs npmScopes in .yarnrc.yml.

## Confirmed non-issue
The `--registry=` flag applies to the whole install, not just the @mms scope, but the Artifactory repo is a virtual repo fronting an npmjs.org remote (docs/jfrog-setup.md:13-20), so transitive deps including `lit` resolve through the proxy.

## Open questions for J
1. `.npmrc.example` line 2 says "FOR CONTRIBUTORS ONLY — consumers do NOT need this file". That becomes wrong under the project-level approach. Update in this ticket, or scope DS-163 to the Storybook guide only?
2. Keep the "if npm prompts for credentials" callout (line 39), or is it redundant once the explicit `npm config delete` prereq exists?

## Not verified
- That the single-line Artifactory install actually succeeds end-to-end — could not test, not on Maximus VPN at time of audit.
- Exact npm error text for a bare `\` argument on Windows (npm-package-arg classifies `\` differently on Windows, where it is a path separator).

## DELIVERED — 5 commits on feature/ds-163-cross-platform-install

1. `fix:` sideEffects gains ./dist/index.js + ./src/index.ts; uss-oh-dvs theme exports added; mms-text-field added to the barrel (it was missing entirely — 28 component files, 27 barrel imports); generate-exports.mjs gains a Phase 4 barrel-completeness check that fails the build if any self-registering component is absent from src/index.ts.
2. `fix!:` @lit/react moved from dependencies to optional peerDependencies; engines field added (node >=20, npm >=10); the entire dependencies block is now deleted — zero runtime dependencies. Consumer install drops from "added 10 packages" to "added 7".
3. `feat:` ./standalone entry point. New Step 4 in scripts/build-package.mjs esbuild-bundles dist/standalone.js with Lit, all 28 components, icons, tokens and all 8 theme/mode sheets inlined. Injects a <style id="mms-design-system-standalone"> and sets data-theme="default" when absent. Theme font directories are deliberately excluded — their @font-face rules carry relative url() that cannot survive inlining.
4. `docs:` new cross-platform Get Started page (02-GetStarted.stories.ts); old page renamed to Installation (Old) with a superseded banner and its stale 0.9.0 version corrected; 03-HTMLUsage standalone section rewritten; storySort updated; false "auto-registers custom elements" claim corrected in src/index.ts. Step 2 "Install Lit" deleted — npm 7+ auto-installs peers, so it was instructing consumers to do something npm already did.
5. `docs:` AI-first README restructure. Quickstart in the first 20 lines, all 28 tag names, the data-theme/data-mode/data-density contract, and an explicit pointer to custom-elements.json as the machine-readable spec.

## POWERSHELL DEFECT — found by testing, in the new guide itself

Decision 6 (install PowerShell rather than reason about Windows behavior) paid for itself immediately. Parse-testing passed all commands on pwsh 7.6.5, but that proves nothing — splatting binds at invocation, not at parse. Argument-delivery testing via /bin/echo showed:

```
written:   npm config set @mms:registry=<url> --location=project
delivered: npm config set =<url> --location=project        <- @mms:registry STRIPPED
written:   npm config get @mms:registry
delivered: npm config get                                  <- argument DROPPED ENTIRELY
```

PowerShell parses `@mms:registry` as splatting the scope-qualified variable `$mms:registry`; `mms` is read as a scope qualifier, the variable is undefined, and the token vanishes before npm sees it. `@mms/design-system` survives because `/` is not a scope separator.

This broke Step 1, the Verify command, and the Troubleshooting `npm config delete` line — the exact class of failure this ticket exists to eliminate, reintroduced in its replacement.

Fix: double-quote every `@mms:`-prefixed argument. Re-tested via argument delivery — all 7 guide commands now arrive byte-identical on pwsh 7.6.5, bash, and zsh, including with a hostile `$mms` variable defined. Added a "Keep the double quotes" callout at Step 1 and a Troubleshooting row for the resulting error.

Symptom verified rather than assumed: npm fails loudly with "`` is not a valid npm option" and writes no .npmrc at all. An earlier draft of the callout claimed it "writes a broken entry" — corrected.

cmd.exe remains untested (no Windows host). Double-quoted arguments are standard there and `@` is not special outside a batch-file line start, but this is reasoned, not measured.

## VALIDATION LADDER

1. Bundle shake — PASS. npm run verify-bundle: Gate 1 single 1.20MB, Gate 2 barrel 1.53MB (was 0 bytes), Gate 3 real Vite build 45.8KB main chunk. Independent esbuild harness: barrel 1,707,258 bytes / 28 mms tags; single 1,341,826 / 2; standalone 1,768,576 / 29; react 1,342,318 / 2.
2. Clean-room install — PASS (VPN, prior session). Project-level .npmrc only, no credentials.
3. Bundler-free page — PASS against the rebuilt standalone. 28/28 elements registered, missing []; 142,631 chars inlined CSS with 8 theme rules; data-theme auto-set to "default"; all 8 theme/mode combos resolve tokens; button background tracks theme (maximus rgb(80,46,145), va-gov rgb(0,113,187), uss-oh-dvs rgb(14,63,117)).
4. PC validation — NOT RUN. Needs the reporting dev's time on Windows. Explicitly unverified.
5. Anonymous read — PASS (VPN, prior session).

Full test suite: 853 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.

Two probe errors worth recording, both mine, both caught before they became conclusions:
- All 6 non-default theme combos initially read (EMPTY). Cause was a stale HTTP cache entry fetched under max-age=3600; a fresh URL resolved it. The build was correct throughout — the probe was wrong.
- Button background appeared frozen across themes. Cause was `transition: background-color` on mms-button:160 — getComputedStyle read immediately after an attribute flip returns the pre-transition value. Re-probed with a 450ms settle.

Also caught in review: the raw backticks in the new Troubleshooting row terminated the lit template literal early (TypeError: html(...) is not a function). Replaced with ` entities and re-verified all three developer-guide pages render with 0 console errors.

## RESOLVED FROM "Open questions for J"
1. .npmrc.example line 2 — left as-is per J (no other contributors today).
2. Credentials callout — kept, and strengthened into an explicit "you never need JFrog credentials" block, since the misleading permissions-flavoured 404 is what sent a consumer's AI hunting for them.

## STILL OPEN
- README previously opened with a table of 10 unpublished @mms/* packages under the line "Packages are not yet published" — actively misleading, since @mms/design-system@0.21.0 is live. Rewritten to state that one package is published and the rest are Phase 4. Flagging because it contradicts CLAUDE.md section 3.2, which still lists the ten as the package architecture.
- Installation (Old) retained pending PC sign-off, then delete.
- Usage-metrics ticket approved by J but not yet created — needs an id.

## COMMIT 6 — auto dark mode (prefers-color-scheme)

`prefers-color-scheme` appeared ZERO times in the codebase. Dark mode was reachable only via an explicit [data-mode="dark"], so every no-JS distribution path (headless CSS, AEM, Drupal, a plain <script> prototype) could not honour the user's OS setting at all.

J's governance call, overriding my proposal to hold this out of scope: "A11y is at the core of all of our projects. dark-mode, light-mode must be supported to ensure we are meeting the right a11y standards. Not accommodating the dark mode is an a11y violation in a broader context of POUR principles." In scope.

Fixed in the token pipeline, not in JavaScript. scripts/build-package.mjs emits a second, media-wrapped copy of each dark block keyed on :not([data-mode]). The two selectors are mutually exclusive by construction, so an explicit data-mode always wins with no JS and no flash. Source stays DRY — duplication happens only in dist/. The transform throws rather than skipping silently if a dark sheet is restructured into multiple blocks.

Known limit, documented as unsupported: data-theme on <html> and data-mode on <body> defeats the override.

## COMMIT 7 — `warning` aliased to `caution` (all four alert components)

`caution` is the alert type whose icon is named `warning`, and `warning` is the more common vocabulary across design systems — so consumers guess it as the attribute value. It is not a valid enum member. On mms-status-tag it was clamped to `success`; on mms-inline-alert, mms-alert-banner and mms-toast it matched no :host([alert-type=…]) block and fell through the icon switch to informational. Either way the author asked for a caution and got a different status, silently.

J approved option 1 (alias) over the alternatives (rename the enum / add a dev warning). New src/utils/normalize-alert-type.ts holds the map; each component resolves it in willUpdate before its own validation. Because alertType reflects, resolving on the property keeps attribute, CSS selector match and icon in agreement. Additive and non-breaking — every existing value behaves exactly as before.

One existing assertion changed: mms-status-tag.test.ts previously asserted `warning` clamps to `success`. That is now the alias case. Four new regression tests; unit suite 1103 -> 1107.

## CONTRAST AUDIT — 4 failures, one root cause (was reported as 5)

Solution B makes every dark palette reachable by default, so all 8 theme x mode combinations were audited with a new scripts/contrast-check.mjs that resolves the rendered var() chain rather than checking palettes in the abstract. 56 checks.

REAL: mms-tabs-item fill active — --color-text-on-emphasis (hardcoded #ffffff) on --color-action-solid (-> --color-primary-9, which inverts to a light tint in dark mode). 4.17-4.19:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement, in all four themes. Same class as DS-108: a foreground held fixed while its background inverts. mms-button avoids it by using the per-theme --color-text-on-primary. `primary` is Tier 1 in all four themes so nothing exempts this pair. FIXED on J's instruction (see COMMIT 8) — mms-tabs-item now uses the per-theme --color-text-on-primary, the same token mms-button already uses to avoid this exact trap. Token mapping only: no primitive hex moved, no shared token repointed or deleted.

WITHDRAWN (mine, incorrect): a fifth finding claimed mms-button color-scheme="secondary" failed at 3.07:1 on va-gov and that the Tier 3 skip in audit:contrast was hiding it. contrast-check.mjs crossed all themes against all pairs without consulting src/config/theme-constraints.ts. INTERACTIVE_COLOR_SCHEMES['va-gov'] is ['primary','onyx','error'] — `secondary` is not an interactive scheme on va-gov, so that is not a supported configuration. The tier system was right; my check was measuring a combination it already excludes. J was correct to push back.

## WHY THE A11Y SUITE DID NOT CATCH THE TABS FAILURE — three independent gaps

1. `npm run audit:contrast` is light-mode only and covers 3 of 4 themes. scripts/contrast-audit.mjs:70-140 holds only default/maximus/va-gov, all light hex, no uss-oh-dvs.
2. The axe suite renders maximus only. .storybook/preview.ts:37 defaults the theme arg to 'maximus' and no a11y test passes a theme argument.
3. Operative gap: tabStyle=fill sits outside the color axis. tests/tabs.a11y.ts:23-27 sets colorProp: null, so forEachColorAxis runs ['default'] and only ever renders `minimal` — the one tab style that does NOT put a label on a solid brand fill. The tests DO run full expectNoA11yViolations in dark mode; they just never render the failing variant.

Structural issue named for J: scripts/audit-a11y-coverage.mjs validates coverage against a hand-written registry declaring what SHOULD be covered, never against the component's real prop surface. `colorProp` models which palette is used; `fill` vs `minimal` changes whether there is a filled background behind the text at all — invisible to that model. Every layer agreed with its neighbour; none was compared to reality. mms-tag's tagStyle (stroke/fill) has the identical hole (audit-a11y-coverage.mjs:275-285). Suggested direction: derive the axis from custom-elements.json, which already lists every attribute and its type union, and require an explicit waiver-with-reason for any enum prop excluded from the color matrix.

## TIER 2/3 ENFORCEMENT IS ADVISORY, NOT BLOCKING

Answering J directly: yes, a consumer can still render <mms-button color-scheme="secondary"> on va-gov today. src/utils/validate-color-scheme.ts:28-58 detects the tier from an empty --color-{scheme}-10 inside a requestAnimationFrame and emits a console.warn — it does not block. Blocking needs a post-render clamp because data-theme lives on an ancestor, which means a brief flash of the non-compliant color. Recommended as its own ticket, not folded in here.

## COMMIT 8 — mms-tabs-item dark contrast fix + contrast-modes CI gate

Token mapping only, per J's approval. mms-tabs-item's fill-active label moves from the fixed-white --color-text-on-emphasis to the per-theme --color-text-on-primary. No primitive hex value moved and no shared token was repointed or deleted (additive-only rule respected).

scripts/contrast-check.mjs also became theme-constraint aware — it now reads src/config/theme-constraints.ts, so 6 theme x scheme pairs a theme never allows move from CHECKED to N/A instead of being measured. That is the fix for the withdrawn va-gov finding above.

Re-measured: checked 50, failures 0, n/a 6, unresolved 0.

`npm run audit:contrast-modes` is now wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml, immediately after the existing audit:contrast step. It was previously a script nobody ran. It is the gate that catches the DS-108 defect class — a foreground token held fixed while its background inverts in dark mode.

## COMMIT 9 — a11y coverage-model gap CLOSED

The structural fix J approved: scripts/audit-a11y-coverage.mjs now DERIVES the colour axis from custom-elements.json rather than trusting a hand-written colorProp declaration.

New concept — the colour-material axis: an enum prop where two of its values pull different sets of colour tokens. Distinct from colorProp, which only models which palette you can pick. colorProp cannot express whether there is a filled background behind the text at all, and that is the question axe answers under SC 1.4.3.

Rule adopted for multiply-vs-waive: MULTIPLY when the axis changes what sits behind text; WAIVE when it only alters an edge, shadow or radius. Two new registry fields — colorAxisMultipliers: [propName] cross-multiplies an extra axis into compound variant names (e.g. stroke-primary), applied after theme/internal exclusion; colorAxisWaivers: { propName: reason } requires a non-empty string, a bare true is ignored rather than honoured.

All 8 flagged axes disposed:
- tabs / tabStyle (fill, minimal) — MULTIPLIED. This was the hole that let the defect ship.
- tag / tagStyle (stroke, fill) — MULTIPLIED.
- tag / colorScheme (4 values) — REGISTERED; colorProp was null.
- stepper / colorScheme (4 values) — REGISTERED; likewise null despite a real reflected @property at mms-stepper.component.ts:75.
- card / surface (tint, solid) — MULTIPLIED; swaps the background under all card text.
- button / variant (primary, secondary, ghost) — MULTIPLIED; ghost puts the label straight on the page background.
- card / variant (4 values) — WAIVED, edge-only (shadow / border / accent bar).
- breadcrumbs / linkColor — WAIVED, pinned to neutral at mms-breadcrumbs.component.ts:153.

Bug found and fixed while doing it: getColorVariants inverted Exclude<> unions. A naive quoted-string regex read Exclude<ColorScheme, 'error'> as ['error'] — the exact inverse of the intent. Delegated to resolveEnumValues; verified behaviour-preserving on every other component.

RESULT — the grid grew by 162 rows and ALL 162 PASS. Playwright: 241 passed, 0 failed (58.4s) across button/card/stepper/tabs/tag. Audit: 791 PASS, 0 FAIL, 475 N/A, 0 PAGE-LEVEL, 5 BUILD GAP, 29 MANUAL. The 5 BUILD GAPs are the pre-existing, already-cited mms-multi-select SC 1.3.5 rows tracked under DS-149 — non-blocking, not introduced here.

mms-tabs-item was the ONLY real defect in the set. Every other newly-rendered axis — tag fill-*, button ghost-* and secondary-* at all four schemes, card tint-*, stepper's whole palette — was already compliant in both modes. My stop-condition (report and stop rather than edit components if real failures surfaced) was therefore not triggered.

Type safety: the new compound variant lists in the test files are derived from the components' own exported unions via `as const satisfies readonly ButtonVariant[]` etc, so a prop union change breaks the build rather than silently shrinking coverage.

## COMMIT 10 — runtime validation reaches the consumer's CI

Answering J directly on CI scope ("If there's a way to influence the consumer's CI, then definitely yes"): our CI cannot catch an invalid theme x scheme combination, because one is only ever produced by a consumer choosing it, in their app, at runtime. The console channel is the only signal that reaches them.

src/utils/validate-color-scheme.ts upgraded from console.warn to console.error. That is the level consumer tooling actually acts on — Vitest/Jest failOnConsole, Playwright console assertions, and the CRA dev overlay all key on error and ignore warn. At warn the message was technically present and practically invisible. Still deduped per theme:colorScheme:component, so a 200-row list logs once.

Verified our own runner does not fail on it: npm run test:unit 29 files / 1107 tests passed. No test asserts on this utility's console output.

## RESOLVED — was OPEN DECISIONS FOR J
1. mms-tabs-item dark contrast fix — FOLDED IN (commit 8), per J.
2. a11y coverage-model gap — FOLDED IN (commit 9), per J. Confirmed to J up front that this is test-writing, not token mapping.
3. Tier 2/3 runtime blocking — still its own ticket, NOT created (consult-first rule). Advisory-only today; upgraded to console.error in commit 10, but it does not clamp. A hard clamp needs a post-render fix because data-theme lives on an ancestor, which means a brief flash.
4. Usage-metrics ticket — created as DS-164, parked in ops, with the DevOps email draft included in the ticket per J.

## COMMIT 11 — contrast-audit.mjs retired; its sweep merged into contrast-check.mjs

verify-gates.mjs recorded scripts/contrast-audit.mjs as DISCONNECTED: it had no imports and read no files, so breaking a real theme colour in src/themes/default.css left all 296 of its checks green. Every value it measured was a hex literal hand-copied into the script — a duplicate of the theme CSS that could drift from it at any time, and had (3 of 4 themes, light mode only).

J's call: fix now, inside DS-163, not as a new ticket. Neither delete nor keep-as-is — MERGE. The breadth was real; the inputs were fiction.

What moved: the combinatorial sweep (every foreground x every background) now runs inside contrast-check.mjs, against the var() chains resolved out of the real src/themes/*.css and src/styles/*.css, across all four themes x both modes. contrast-audit.mjs deleted; the duplicate audit:contrast-modes npm alias deleted; npm run audit:contrast now runs contrast-check.mjs; ci.yml collapses two steps into one; verify-gates.mjs's two cases collapse into one and its expectDisconnected case is gone.

ADJACENCY MODEL — the part that makes the sweep usable. A raw cross-product manufactures failures: it pairs a control's border against a fill that lives inside that same control, which no screen renders. Measured here, 33 of 37 sweep failures were exactly that — an 18x over-report, and precisely the kind of output people learn to ignore. Each background now declares a role (container = the Page/Surface a control is placed ON, steps 1/2; element = a fill INSIDE a container, step 3) and each foreground group declares which roles it can sit against: text -> both, border -> container only (SC 1.4.11 measures a boundary against what surrounds it), fill -> both. Both maps are exhaustive by assertion, so adding a group or a role without deciding its adjacency throws rather than silently widening or narrowing coverage. Skipped pairs are counted and printed as "not adjacent", never dropped silently.

ONE REAL DEFECT, isolated by measurement: --color-action-text was bound to --color-primary-9. Step 9 is Solid (anchor) — a fill you place text ON, not a text colour. It measured 4.19-4.50:1 against a 4.5 floor. J identified the correct target from the framework before I did ("if it's a text matter, then shouldn't we use step 12?"); step 12 is Text, step 11 is Text muted. Repointed to step 12 across all 8 theme sheets plus src/styles/tokens-semantic.css, each with a comment stating why step 9 was wrong. No component consumes --color-action-text today, so there is no visual change — this is the contract being made correct before something depends on it.

Isolation runs proving the two findings are independent, not one masking the other:
  as authored               1080 checked, 37 below floor
  action-text -> step 12    1080 checked,  4 below floor
  adjacency only            1056 checked, 33 below floor
  both                      1056 checked,  0 below floor

DOC DEFECTS FIXED IN THE SAME PASS — docs/color-palette-generation.md was the source of the step-9 error and was itself wrong. Its role table collapsed 9-10 into "Solids" and 11-12 into "Text colors" with no per-step names, and its Tier 1/2 generation blocks labelled step 11 "Text" and step 12 "Dark text", contradicting the canonical map in src/stories/foundations/Colors.stories.ts (stepPurposes). Corrected to name every step, cross-reference the canonical map, and state in bold that steps 9/10 are fills you place text on. Added a "why steps 1 and 2 only, and not step 3" rationale to Constraint 2 matching the ADJACENCY model. Its restatement of PALETTE_TIERS / VALID_COLOR_SCHEMES was also stale (missing the error scheme and the uss-oh-dvs theme) — resynced against the real src/config/theme-constraints.ts.

Also updated: .claude/contracts/a11y-coverage.md (its "Known gap — no dark-mode table" paragraph is obsolete; that gap is closed), .claude/skills/a11y-test/SKILL.md, and docs/ds-163-validation-2026-08-20.md.

RESULT — pairs 58 checked / 0 failures / 14 n-a / 0 unresolved; sweep 1408 checked / 0 failures / 32 not adjacent. verify-gates: 8 LIVE, 0 INERT, 0 DISCONNECTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE, 1 SKIPPED, PASS (was 7 LIVE / 1 DISCONNECTED / 1 UNVERIFIABLE / FAIL).

SECOND TOKEN OF THE SAME CLASS — fixed on J's correction:
- --color-action-text-hover was bound to --color-primary-10 (Solid hovered) — another fill step used as text. It passed 4.5:1 by measurement (worst case 5.74:1), so it was a modelling error, not a contrast failure, and the sweep never saw it because hover variants were absent from SWEEP_FOREGROUNDS.
- I first reported this as a design decision, reasoning that with resting text at step 12 (the darkest step) there was no darker step to hover to. J: "you have lost your ability to apply a simple critical thinking. if you review our color framework, step 11, text muted can also be considered as a 'hover' for text, no?" — correct. Hover need not darken. Steps 11 (Text muted) and 12 (Text) are both text steps; hover moves within the text band. This is the third recurrence of the same failure mode in this ticket: reasoning from measurement or from an assumed rule instead of reading the role map first.
- Repointed to var(--color-primary-11) across all eight theme sheets and src/styles/tokens-semantic.css, with a comment naming the step and stating why a fill step is never the hover target for text.
- Closed the gap that hid it: --color-action-text-hover, --color-action-stroke-hover and --color-action-solid-hover added to SWEEP_FOREGROUNDS. An unmeasured hover state is exactly where a fill step gets bound to a text role and survives review. Sweep goes 1056 -> 1408 checks, 0 failures, 32 not adjacent.

FALSE "auto-generated" HEADERS — fixed on J's approval:
- All three Layer 0/1/2 sheets (src/styles/tokens-primitives.css, tokens-structural.css, tokens-semantic.css) opened with "Do not edit directly, this file was auto-generated." False in every case. Verified: every reference to these paths across scripts/ is a read — validate-tokens.mjs, generate-token-mapping.mjs, contrast-check.mjs read them; build-package.mjs:59-63 only copies them verbatim into dist/. Nothing writes them.
- Root cause of the claim: style-dictionary is a devDependency (package.json:260) with no config file, no token source directory, and no script that invokes it. The Style Dictionary pipeline in CLAUDE.md section 3.4 is still ahead of us, not behind us. The headers were aspirational, not stale output.
- Harm: the header instructs the next reader — human or AI — not to touch a file they are in fact supposed to edit, and to go hunting for a generator that does not exist. I hand-edited tokens-semantic.css twice in this ticket, directly against its own stated rule.
- Fixed all three rather than only the one flagged: fixing one and leaving two identical copies is a patchfix. Each header now states the layer's purpose, that it is hand-maintained, and that build-package.mjs only copies it. tokens-primitives.css carries the explanation of why the old claim existed and notes that the header is the thing that should become true again once the pipeline lands. tokens-semantic.css additionally states that every step binding must match the role map in Colors.stories.ts and that contrast-check.mjs gates it.
- Comment-only. validate-tokens 753 references PASS; contrast 58 pairs + 1408 sweep, 0 failures; verify-gates 8 LIVE, PASS.

## STILL OPEN AFTER THIS TICKET
- Consumer-side ESLint rule — SPLIT OUT AS DS-165, parked in post-mvp1 per J. Opt-in by construction: an ESLint plugin only runs if the consumer extends it, so it reaches good devs only. TypeScript types would be auto-consumed but cannot work (the theme is ambient — the compiler cannot correlate a button's colorScheme with the root element's data-theme); postinstall is automatic but hostile and often blocked in enterprise CI. The runtime console.error shipped in commit 10 is the only universal net, which is why the lint rule is polish rather than the primary fix.
- Ladder 4 (PC dev walks the new guide on Windows) — explicitly unverified, gated on his time.
- CLAUDE.md section 3.2 still lists ten @mms/* packages and contradicts the rewritten README. One-word fix, own branch.
- Installation (Old) retained pending PC sign-off, then delete.

title: Measure @mms/design-system adoption — Artifactory usage stats + repo scanning
notes:
Raised out of DS-163 (NPM distribution strategy review, 2026-08-20). J: "We'll grab the latest available ticket number, and park it in ops."

We publish @mms/design-system to JFrog Artifactory and have zero visibility into who consumes it. This ticket covers getting that visibility.

=== CURRENT STATE — AWAITING DEVOPS (2026-08-31) ===

The email was sent to Sunil on 2026-08-31. Nothing further can start until he replies. Parked here deliberately; the ticket stays in-progress rather than moving to pending-review or done, because the deliverable is the access itself, not the email.

=== WHAT WAS SENT ===

Four asks, not the five drafted below. Ask 5 (deploy permission on artifactory-build-info) was deliberately left out: its only unique value is Xray build-level scanning, and whether Xray is licensed is exactly what ask 4 asks. Revisit it only if ask 4 comes back with a license.

The sent version was also reframed away from the prescriptive draft below. J's direction: state what we need and ask Sunil how to get there, rather than explaining Artifactory to the Artifactory admin. The two sample API calls and the mechanism commentary ("stats collection is disabled in some configurations", "AQL stat.* requires elevated privileges", "worth two minutes of checking") were all cut for that reason.

Substance of what went out: ahead of the v1 release we need to report on adoption and have no visibility today. What we need to be able to answer is how many teams are consuming the package, which versions they are on, whether that is growing, and ideally unique consumers rather than raw download counts — CI pipelines can pull the same version hundreds of times, so a download number alone could mislead. We do not know what the instance already supports, so the question put to Sunil is what he would suggest. A read-only account or token scoped to this one repo is fine; we are not asking for write access or any change to the publish pipeline. If something already licensed covers it, better still.

One paragraph was cut by J immediately before sending: the flag that short log retention should be extended before we start measuring. Still true — retention cannot be recovered retroactively — and worth raising directly if retention turns out to be the binding constraint.

=== WHY REGISTRY STATS ARE PRIMARY, NOT SECONDARY ===

Repo scanning only sees repos we can read. The flaw J named directly: we don't know what orgs exist that we don't have access to — and those are exactly the adopters most worth knowing about, because they found the package without us.

Artifactory sees every consumer unconditionally. Anyone who installs hits the registry, whether they're in digital-dxhub, another Maximus org, a contractor environment, or a laptop we'll never hear about. That makes it the only complete source.

  PRIMARY       Artifactory stats — how many installs, which versions, how many
                distinct consumers, trend over time. Coverage: everyone.
  SUPPLEMENTARY Repo scanning (gh search code) — which components are used, how
                often, which are dead. Coverage: only repos we can read.

Repo scanning is not worthless — it is the only thing that answers "is anyone using mms-tag?", which drives deprecation. But it cannot answer "who uses this?" and should not be sold as if it can. It is depth on a subset, not breadth.

Runtime telemetry is REJECTED. A component library that phones home, installed on government sites handling Medicaid data, is a compliance conversation that would stall adoption and deserve to. Marina didn't do it either.

=== MARINA PRECEDENT — WHY THE ACCESS REQUEST GOES FIRST ===

Marina's ds-metrics skill (ui-kit/.claude/skills/ds-metrics/skill.md) carries a commented-out block at lines 69-80 listing precisely these metrics — usage by version, unique consumers, projects per consumer, assets used, last use date — annotated "blocked pending Nexus admin access or IQ Server".

It stayed blocked. Marina never got numbers. The lesson is to make the access request NOW, while DevOps is already engaged on Artifactory from DS-089, rather than build a scanner against access we may never get.

=== ORIGINAL FIVE-ASK DRAFT — SUPERSEDED, KEPT FOR REFERENCE ===

This is the version drafted before the 2026-08-31 review. It was NOT sent. It is retained because asks 1-3 name the specific Artifactory mechanisms we will need if Sunil comes back asking what exactly we want, and ask 5 records the build-info 403 finding. Note the sample GET URL below names 0.21.0, which was already stale at send time — the latest published version is 0.23.0.

Subject: Artifactory usage-statistics access for mms-ds-platform

We publish @mms/design-system to the mms-ds-platform virtual repo (backed by mms-ds-platform-local). We need to report adoption — how many teams are consuming it, which versions, and whether usage is growing. We have no visibility today.

Five asks, roughly in order of value:

1. Confirm download statistics are being collected on mms-ds-platform-local.
In some configurations stats collection is disabled for performance. Please confirm it's on, and tell us the date it was enabled — that's the start of our usable history.

2. Grant a read-only account or access token that can query the statistics API.
Specifically, these two calls need to return data rather than 403:

  GET /artifactory/api/storage/mms-ds-platform-local/@mms/design-system/-/design-system-0.21.0.tgz?stats

  POST /artifactory/api/search/aql
  items.find({"repo":"mms-ds-platform-local"}).include("name","created","stat.downloads","stat.downloaded_by")

The AQL stat.* fields require elevated privileges in several Artifactory versions — that is usually the blocker. A dedicated read-only service account scoped to this one repo is fine; we don't need admin.

3. Tell us what request-log retention we have, and whether we can query or export it.
artifactory-request.log is the only thing that distinguishes unique consumers from total downloads — CI pipelines can inflate download counts by orders of magnitude. We need to know: how long logs are retained, whether they're shipped anywhere queryable (Splunk, ELK, S3), and whether we can get read access. If retention is short, we'd like it extended before we start measuring, since we can't recover history retroactively.

4. Tell us whether this instance has JFrog Xray, Insight, or Curation licensed.
If any of these are available they provide usage dashboards directly and asks 1-3 may be partly redundant.

5. Grant deploy permission on the artifactory-build-info repository for our publish identity.
This one is the opposite direction from asks 1-4: those are read access to find out who consumes the package, this is write access to record what produced it. Our publish process wants to attach build-info to each release — the commit SHA it was built from, the runtime, and the resolved dependency graph. Probed on 2026-08-27 with our current token: npm publish works, uploading generic artifacts works, but PUT /api/build returns 403. The JFrog CLI (jf rt build-publish) writes through that same endpoint, so it is a permission grant we need, not a tool we are missing.

We already store the commit and checksum facts as ordinary files alongside the package, so nothing is broken today. What the grant adds is a proper Builds entry in the JFrog UI and, if ask 4 turns up an Xray license, build-level scanning — Xray reads build-info.

=== WHAT TO DO WITH THE ANSWERS ===

Stats collection plus read access alone give downloads per version over time — enough to report an adoption trend. Log retention is what upgrades that to a defensible unique-consumers number. An existing Xray/Insight/Curation license might make the whole thing a dashboard someone already paid for.

Build-info deploy permission stands alone — no part of adoption measurement depends on it, and nothing breaks without it. It was cut from the send rather than dropped from the ticket.

=== VERSION ATTRIBUTION — ALREADY SOLVED, DON'T BREAK IT ===

Releases already carry a stable, greppable marker. custom-elements.json is versioned with the package, so a scan can attribute usage to a specific version with no new instrumentation. Nothing to build; the standing rule is simply DON'T REMOVE IT.

=== SCOPE ===

1. Send the email to DevOps. DONE 2026-08-31 — awaiting Sunil's reply.
2. Once access lands: script the API calls into a repeatable report. BLOCKED on 1.
3. Separately, a gh search code scanner over readable orgs for per-component usage (depth layer). Independent of 1-2 — can start any time.

=== RELATED ===

DS-089 (done) — JFrog registry setup. This is its natural follow-up while DevOps is still engaged.
DS-121 — anonymous read verified passing on VPN 2026-08-20.
DS-163 — the distribution strategy review that raised this.
DS-169 — org migration. Its Phase 7 found the build-info 403 and added the (now unsent) fifth ask. The workaround it shipped (publish-evidence, which writes an SBOM and a provenance file beside the package) means that ask is an improvement, not a blocker.
A separate defect surfaced during this ticket's email review and was fixed inside it: package.json repository.url pointed at the nonexistent maximus-inc org. Corrected to maximus-atx-ce in PR #5 (7b3fbe7). The published 0.23.0 packument still carries the dead URL — it reaches consumers on the next publish, not on that merge.

title: Ship an opt-in ESLint plugin for invalid theme x colorScheme combinations
notes:
Split out of DS-163 per J. Parked in post-mvp1 deliberately — see the priority note at the end, this is polish on top of a net that already catches everyone.

## The problem

A consumer can write <mms-button color-scheme="secondary"> on the va-gov theme today and get a component rendered from a Tier 3 palette that lacks step 10 (hover state). INTERACTIVE_COLOR_SCHEMES['va-gov'] is ['primary','onyx','error'] (src/config/theme-constraints.ts). Nothing stops them at author time.

Our CI cannot catch this. An invalid combination is only ever produced by a consumer choosing one, in their app. Their CI never sees our source; our CI never sees their markup.

## Why not the alternatives — decided in DS-163, recorded so it is not re-litigated

1. TypeScript types. Would be auto-consumed with zero opt-in, which is exactly what we want, but it cannot work here. The theme is AMBIENT — data-theme sits on a root element, often in a different file, sometimes injected at runtime. The compiler has no way to correlate "this button's colorScheme" with "that page's theme." This is a real structural limit, not an implementation shortcut. Do not revisit expecting a different answer.

2. postinstall script. Automatic, and a bad idea. Frequently blocked outright in enterprise CI, and a package that runs code on install reads as hostile — a poor look for a government-facing design system.

3. Runtime console.error. The only genuinely universal net: every consumer gets it, no opt-in, no config. ALREADY SHIPPED in DS-163 — src/utils/validate-color-scheme.ts was upgraded from console.warn to console.error precisely because error is the level consumer tooling acts on (Vitest/Jest failOnConsole, Playwright console assertions, the CRA dev overlay all key on error and ignore warn).

## What this ticket is

An ESLint plugin, and it is OPT-IN by construction. There is no mechanism to force a lint rule on a consumer at import time — they install the plugin and extend it in their own config, or they don't. Only teams that go looking will get it.

The value is timing, not coverage: lint catches the mistake in the editor, before the code runs. The runtime console.error already catches it for everyone, just later.

Rough scope:
- New bin or exported config, e.g. @mms/design-system/eslint-plugin
- Rule reads src/config/theme-constraints.ts (or a generated JSON of it) as its source of truth so the rule cannot drift from the tier system
- Handles the ambient-theme problem the only way lint can: a configurable theme option in the consumer's eslint config ("this project is va-gov"), since static analysis has the same blind spot TypeScript does
- Covers JSX/TSX and plain HTML template literals

## Priority rationale

The runtime error reaches 100% of consumers with zero opt-in. The lint rule reaches only teams that opt in, and tells them the same thing earlier. Worth building; worth not over-investing in. That is why it is post-mvp1 and low, not blocked or urgent.

title: Package-wide enum-membership validation for string properties
notes:
Split out of DS-163 per J (Option C: clamp alert-type now, generalise later). Sibling of DS-165 — that one catches invalid theme x colorScheme pairs, this one catches any string property set to a value outside its declared union.

## The problem

Every @property({ type: String }) typed as a union arrives at runtime as an unvalidated string. TypeScript checks the property assignment in a consumer's .ts file; it checks nothing about an HTML attribute, a value from an API, a CMS field, or a framework binding. Setting alert-type="warn" or variant="primaryy" produces no error anywhere — the component matches no :host([attr=...]) block and falls through to whatever the CSS base case happens to be.

Inventory at time of writing: 28 components, 55 enum-typed @property declarations.

## Why the failure mode varies, and why that matters for priority

Two distinct visibilities, and they should not be treated the same:

- VISIBLE-WRONG. alert-type on mms-status-tag / mms-inline-alert / mms-alert-banner / mms-toast. An invalid value renders a plausible-looking component carrying the WRONG STATUS — an author asking for an error alert gets an informational one. Nothing looks broken. This is why DS-163 clamped these four rather than waiting for this ticket: 4 of 28 components, ~7% of the surface, but the highest-consequence 7%.
- INVISIBLE-DEGRADED. Most of the rest (variant, size, tabStyle, surface, ...). An invalid value renders unstyled or default-styled — obviously off to anyone looking at it, and it does not misrepresent meaning.

DS-163 also upgraded validate-color-scheme.ts from console.warn to console.error, for the same reason: error is the level consumer tooling actually acts on.

## What this ticket is

One generic mechanism replacing the prospect of 55 hand-written runtime guards. Rough shape, to be designed rather than prescribed here:

- A decorator or a small base-class hook, e.g. @enumProperty({ values: [...], fallback: '...' }) or a validated() companion to @property, so the allowed set is declared ONCE next to the property rather than restated in a willUpdate body
- Clamp to the property default (never leave the invalid value in place — it reflects, so the attribute, CSS and any icon lookup must all agree). See src/utils/normalize-alert-type.ts for the pattern DS-163 established, including alias resolution (warning -> caution) ahead of the clamp
- Emit a console.error naming the component, the property, the offending value and the accepted set. Author-time catching is this ticket's job; the four DS-163 clamps deliberately stay SILENT so they do not double-report once this lands
- Zero cost when the value is valid — this runs on every property set on every component
- Audit script or unit test asserting every enum-typed @property in src/ is covered, so the mechanism cannot silently fall behind new components (same anti-drift principle as scripts/generate-exports.mjs's barrel check)

## Sequencing note

When this lands, revisit the four alert-type components: their per-component willUpdate guards and the FALLBACK_ALERT_TYPE constants should collapse into the generic mechanism, and normalize-alert-type.ts should survive only if the warning -> caution alias still needs a home the generic mechanism does not provide.

title: Ship Avenir Next brand fonts with the package
notes:
Raised out of DS-163, which found that no brand font ever loaded on any consumption path.

## What DS-163 found

`dist/themes/<brand>/index.css` shipped 5 @font-face rules pointing at `../../assets/fonts/<brand>/*.woff2`, but `find dist -name '*.woff2'` returned 0 — no font binary has ever been in the published package. The sheets were also unreachable: the exports map has no `./themes/<brand>/index.css` key, so nothing could import them even when present. Every consumer rendered a fallback face while the package claimed otherwise.

## What DS-163 did about it

Stopped shipping the dead sheets (removed the `themeDirs` copy from `scripts/build-package.mjs`) and made the fallback deterministic instead of accidental: the Maximus stack became `'Avenir Next LT Pro', Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif` rather than falling through to `system-ui`, which resolves to a different face per OS (San Francisco / Segoe UI / Roboto) and made the brand look different on every platform. Documented on the Storybook Themes page as an explicit contract: a theme names its typeface, it does not carry the file.

That is a correct resting state, not a workaround. This ticket is the upgrade.

## Scope decision — licensing is the consumer's responsibility (J, 2026-08-31)

This ticket originally treated file provenance as its blocker: the existing `src/assets/fonts/maximus/*.woff2` were converted out of the Adobe Creative Cloud livetype cache, and the ticket's first two steps were to locate the Maximus Avenir Next purchase record and re-source webfonts from that vendor.

Those steps are **removed, not deferred.** The platform is not the delivery vehicle for an MMS-branded product — it is the substrate delivery teams build on. When a team takes on a Maximus-branded engagement, that team secures its own font licensing. The platform ships the reference brand implementation; the consumer owns the entitlement for their deployment. No Brand approval is required for the platform to carry these files.

## Source

Three candidate files were provided and evaluated:

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `webfonts/2AA003_{0,1}_0.{eot,ttf,woff}` | **Rejected.** Internal names `AvenirLTPro-Light` / `AvenirLTPro-Medium` — Avenir LT Pro is a different typeface from Avenir Next, not a naming variant. Two weights, no italic, no woff2, dated 2014. |
| `Avenir.ttc` | **Rejected.** Family is Avenir, not Avenir Next. |
| `Avenir Next.ttc` | **Selected.** 12 faces, ver 13.0d1e10, vendor LINO. Covers Regular / Medium / Bold / Italic — the exact four faces the repo declares. |

Provenance stated plainly: the two `.ttc` files match the version, vendor, copyright and table set of the copies in `/System/Library/Fonts/` — they are macOS system font copies, not a vendor-issued webfont kit. Recorded here so it is not later mistaken for a Monotype delivery.

The raw `.ttc` files are **not committed** — 6.6MB of conversion source with no runtime role. SHA-256 checksums and per-face version metadata go in `src/assets/fonts/maximus/README.md` so any shipped woff2 can be reconciled against the source binary later.

## Drift analysis — measured, not assumed

Comparing the outgoing CC-cache woff2 against the faces extracted from `Avenir Next.ttc`:

- **Advance widths** — identical across all 374 shared codepoints except 7 non-text ones (NUL, CR, Δ, Ω, μ, π, U+F8FF). Horizontal metrics do not move.
- **Kerned line width** — 8 representative UI strings simulated through flattened GPOS PairPos. 0.000% difference on 7 of 8; worst case +0.097% (+0.32px at 16px). No reflow risk.
- **Outline shape** — Hausdorff deviation maxes at 8.22–9.19 units per 1000em (0.13px at 16px), median 1.03–1.93. Sub-pixel; not perceptible.
- **Coverage** — the TTC adds 602 codepoints (Cyrillic, Greek, Latin Extended Additional) and loses exactly one (U+0237, dotless j, in Medium only).

Method was control-tested rather than trusted: comparing the current Bold against the TTC's **Demi Bold** produced 78/85 advance-width differences and 84 bbox differences, proving the comparison detects a wrong weight. The zero-drift result against Bold is therefore meaningful, not a false negative.

## The one real regression, and its fix

Vertical metrics differ. The current files carry hhea 978/-250/0 (a 1.228em line box); the TTC faces carry 1000/-366/0 (1.366em). Left uncorrected the swap grows every Maximus line box by 11.2% and moves the baseline — **including where `line-height` is explicitly set**, because half-leading derives from ascent+descent.

Fix is the pattern already in this repo from DS-156 (Source Sans 3 normalized to Source Sans Pro's metrics). Every Maximus `@font-face` block gets:

```
ascent-override: 97.8%;
descent-override: 25%;
line-gap-override: 0%;
```

This is mandatory, not optional — without it the swap is a visible typographic regression across every Maximus-themed surface.

**These are hhea values, not the OS/2 typo table — and the first pass got that wrong.** The outgoing files do set `USE_TYPO_METRICS` (typo 758/-242/200, a 1.200em box), so normalizing to the typo metrics looks correct on paper, and that is what this ticket originally shipped. Chromium on macOS ignores the flag and reads hhea, so 1.200em is not what those files ever rendered: measured live, the typo-based overrides left a 1-3px baseline shift between 14px and 24px while box heights matched, which is why reading tables alone did not catch it. Caught in QA before commit — see the QA section below.

## Family rename

The TTC's actual family name is `Avenir Next`, not `Avenir Next LT Pro`. Since the LT Pro files are no longer the source, the declared name changes to match reality. Affects `src/assets/fonts/font-faces.css`, `src/themes/maximus.css`, `src/themes/maximus-dark.css`, `src/themes/maximus/index.css`, `src/stories/developer-guide/05-Themes.stories.ts`, `src/stories/foundations/Typography.stories.ts`. The historical entry in `WhatsNew.stories.ts` stays as written — it records what was true at the time.

## Work

1. Convert `Avenir Next.ttc` Regular / Medium / Bold / Italic to woff2 at full coverage, replacing `src/assets/fonts/maximus/*.woff2` (filenames follow the rename).
2. Rename the family to `Avenir Next` across the six files above, and add the three metric overrides to all four Maximus `@font-face` blocks in both `font-faces.css` and `src/themes/maximus/index.css`.
3. Rewrite `src/assets/fonts/maximus/README.md` with real provenance, source checksums, per-face versions, and the conversion command — it currently reads "Adobe Fonts subscription required", which this ticket makes untrue.
4. Ship fonts in the package: copy `src/assets/fonts/` to `dist/assets/fonts/` (the existing `../../assets/fonts/...` URLs in the theme sheets then resolve unchanged from `dist/themes/<brand>/`), restore the theme-subdirectory copy in `scripts/build-package.mjs`, and add an exports entry so consumers can reach it — `./fonts.css` pointing at the combined `src/assets/fonts/font-faces.css`, matching Marina's `./fonts.css`.
5. Have the CLI-scaffolded `index.html` link it, so `npx mms-ds start` gives real brand typography with zero setup.
6. Update the Themes page Typography section and `src/assets/fonts/font-faces.css`'s header, which currently asserts the opposite stance ("These fonts are NOT bundled with NPM packages").

## Note — the OFL brands were never blocked

`va-gov` (Source Sans Pro, Roboto Mono) and `uss-oh-dvs` (Source Sans 3) are OFL 1.1 / Apache 2.0 — explicitly redistributable and self-hostable, ~492K combined. They ship alongside Avenir in step 4; no separate rollout is needed now that Avenir is unblocked.

## Outcome

Done as a straight swap: same four faces, same family role, new source files, family renamed, plus the packaging that makes the files actually reach a consumer.

**The swap.** `src/assets/fonts/maximus/avenir-next-{regular,medium,bold,italic}.woff2` replace the four `avenir-next-lt-pro-*` files. Family renamed to `Avenir Next` in `font-faces.css`, `themes/maximus.css`, `themes/maximus-dark.css`, `themes/maximus/index.css`, `05-Themes.stories.ts`, `Typography.stories.ts`. All four Maximus `@font-face` blocks in both `font-faces.css` and `themes/maximus/index.css` carry `ascent-override: 97.8% / descent-override: 25% / line-gap-override: 0%`, so the line box stays 1.228em and nothing on a Maximus surface moves. Nothing else about those sheets changed — fallback stacks, token names and values are untouched.

**The packaging (steps 4-5).** `scripts/build-package.mjs` copies `src/assets/fonts/` to `dist/assets/fonts/` and fails the build if that tree contains no woff2, so the DS-163 defect cannot silently recur. `package.json` gains a `./fonts.css` export pointing at the copied `font-faces.css`. The CLI-scaffolded page links it, so `npx mms-ds start` renders real brand type with zero setup.

Step 4's "restore the theme-subdirectory copy" was not done. Those sheets set `--font-family-*` on a bare `:root` rather than `[data-theme="…"]`, so shipping two would have the last one loaded win globally; the set is also incomplete and nothing imports them. `font-faces.css` is the manifest instead — one sheet, every brand, no token side effects.

**Second dead reference, folded in at J's direction.** `va-gov`'s `--font-family-tabular` names Roboto Mono and both woff2 have always been in the repo, but `font-faces.css` never declared them — so on the shipping path every va-gov code block, inline code and figure fell through to `ui-monospace`. Same defect as DS-163's, in the one place DS-163 did not look. Making this sheet the real manifest surfaced it. Two `@font-face` blocks added, no metric override: typo and hhea agree (2146/-555/0, 1.319em), so `USE_TYPO_METRICS` is moot, and this face is not normalizing against a predecessor the way Source Sans 3 is. Declared and shipped font sets now reconcile exactly: 13 of 13.

Verification: `npm run build` and `npm run build-storybook` pass; `npx mms-ds init` scaffolds a page linking `./dist/assets/fonts/font-faces.css`; every declared `url()` resolves against the built `dist/`.

## QA — what the verification pass found

Run at J's request before commit, on the question "is there drift or regression?". Two real findings, both fixed.

**1. The metric overrides were wrong.** Derived from the outgoing faces' OS/2 typo table (758/-242/200) because those faces set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`. Chromium on macOS ignores that flag and reads hhea (978/-250/0), so the typo box is not what the outgoing files rendered — normalizing to it left the box height correct but the baseline 1-3px high across 14-24px. Corrected to 97.8% / 25% / 0% and re-measured: 4 faces × 8 sizes × 11 line-heights = 352 combinations, box height and baseline identical to the outgoing files on every row, zero mismatches.

This was only findable by measuring. Reading the tables produced a confident, internally consistent, wrong answer — the flag is genuinely set, the arithmetic genuinely works out to 1.200em, and no engine involved actually does that.

Consequence worth recording: the outgoing files rendered differently on engines that honor the flag than on the ones that don't. An explicit override applies everywhere, so this also removes that pre-existing platform split — at the cost of matching the honoring engines' old appearance. Normalizing to what our reference engine actually rendered is the defensible target, but it is a choice, not a neutral fix.

**2. The reported width figure was understated.** The 0.097% worst case came from simulating kerning through flattened GPOS. Measured live in Chromium across 8 UI strings × 4 faces, 30 of 32 rows are exactly identical and the worst case is +0.256% (+0.172px at 16px, "Continue" in Medium and Bold). Still far below a reflow threshold, but the honest number is 0.26%, not 0.097%.

**Local CI gate:** 16/16 pass, 2m 21s. A first run failed 949 a11y specs — every one on `net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT` at `localhost:6697`, which Chromium blocks. `derivePort()` in `scripts/run-ci.mjs` picks from 6200-6899, a range containing Chromium's blocked ports (6665-6669, 6697), and hashes the repo path — so this worktree hits it deterministically, and any other worktree whose path hashes into that set will too. Pre-existing harness defect, unrelated to this ticket, not fixed here; worked around with an explicit `STORYBOOK_PORT`. Worth its own ticket.

**3. `docs/fonts.md` was stale, and shipped a harmful snippet.** Not in the ticket's six-file rename list, so the sweep missed it. It documented the four deleted `avenir-next-lt-pro-*` filenames, the old `Avenir Next LT Pro` family, a "Source: Adobe Fonts (subscription)" line contradicting the licensing scope above, and stale byte sizes for the OFL faces (Source Sans 3 listed at 15 KB, actually ~103 KB).

The damaging part was the `@font-face` Reference section: a copy-pasteable Maximus block carrying **no metric overrides**. Anyone following the doc rather than importing `fonts.css` would reproduce the exact 11.2% line-box regression this ticket exists to prevent. The Source Sans 3 block had the same omission against DS-156's overrides — pre-existing, fixed in the same pass rather than leaving one copy-paste regression standing next to a fixed one.

Added a pointer to `@mms/design-system/fonts.css` so consumers import the manifest instead of hand-authoring rules at all.

**Live load verification.** The swap was also confirmed end-to-end in Storybook rather than by build success alone, because Avenir Next is a macOS system font — a broken `url()` would fall back to the system copy and look correct. All six Maximus + Roboto Mono requests return 200, every face reports `loaded`, and the canary measurement reads 98 ascent / 25 descent = 1.23em, matching the declared overrides rather than the system face's 1.366em. Roboto Mono now resolves on the va-gov path for the first time. `dist/` carries 13 of 13 woff2 plus `font-faces.css`.

4. **Third QA round (J: "is everything fixed now?") — two more doc defects, both in files the second round had already rewritten.** (a) `docs/fonts.md` documented the Maximus fallback stack as `system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`, but the sheet that actually ships (`src/themes/maximus.css`) uses `Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif` — and its own comment explicitly argues against `system-ui` because it resolves to a different face per OS. The second round renamed the family in that table row without checking the adjacent column. Corrected, with the rationale written into the doc so it is not "fixed" back. VA.gov and USS OH-DVS rows were verified to match their live sheets exactly; Maximus was the sole mismatch. (b) `src/assets/fonts/maximus/README.md` claimed the family is declared in both `font-faces.css` and `src/themes/maximus/index.css`. The latter is orphaned — no importer, absent from the `package.json` exports map, and its own header points at a nonexistent `@mms/theme-maximus` package. Reworded to name `font-faces.css` as the live declaration site and mark `index.css` as kept in sync defensively. **`src/themes/maximus/index.css` being dead code is pre-existing scaffolding, left in place — removing or wiring it up is out of scope and needs J's call.**

5. **`npm run ci` red on this branch is a CI infrastructure defect, not a regression — root-caused and proven.** The run tested `f413f86b` (main's tip) because the branch has no commits yet, and reported "28 uncommitted file(s) were not included" — so none of DS-167's work was in it. 13/16 gates passed; `test:a11y` failed with 949 of 952 specs unexpected and 0 expected, with `audit:a11y-coverage` and `verify-gates` failing as cascades off it. That all-fail signature is a connection failure, not accessibility findings. The scan loop skips them; an explicitly-set `STORYBOOK_PORT` on the list now fails fast with a named `ERR_UNSAFE_PORT` message instead of burning ten minutes on timeouts.    (a) **`custom-elements.json` churn — root-caused and gated.** `cem analyze` emits the top-level `modules` array in glob-walk order, which is not stable between runs, so two consecutive runs against unchanged source produced a ~5,000-line diff whose content is byte-identical once sorted. The file is tracked and published, so this dirtied the working tree after every build on every machine — 36 commits touched it, most carrying no content change — and every clean-tree-dependent skill (`/publish-storybook`, `/publish-npm`) tripped over it. The plugin itself was resolved to this branch's version, which is a strict superset of main's: main's sorts unguarded, so a missing or duplicate `path` would silently reintroduce undefined ordering. What is genuinely new to this ticket is the enforcement — the guards, `scripts/check-manifest-order.mjs`, the `validate:manifest-order` step, and the `verify-gates.mjs` mutation case. `main` has no gate on the plugin today, so deleting it there fails nothing.

   (b) **CI gate ledger was written into the wrong worktree — real data loss.** `run-ci.mjs` derived its record directory from the script's own location, so a gate invoked from a ticket worktree wrote the record there. Two facts make that destructive: a ledger record is only ever committed from `main` (CLAUDE.md §8 — main-branch allowlist, enforced by `.husky/pre-commit`), and `/pr-merge` Gate 7 deletes the ticket worktree. So the provenance of a gated commit was destroyed before it could ever be recorded. It also falsified the ledger's own rule 3 ("one file per sha, written once, never touched again"): `f413f86b` existed simultaneously in two checkouts with contradictory records — `branch: "main"`, 0 excluded, 12:47 in the primary; `branch: "feature/ds-167-avenir-font-sourcing"`, 30 excluded, 17:30 here. One file per sha only holds if there is one directory. **Amended post-rebase — this ticket ships none of the fix.** `main` fixed the same defect in PR #4, and main's resolver is the better one: `mainWorktree()` reads `git worktree list --porcelain`, whose first entry is the main worktree by definition. This branch's `ledgerRoot()` took `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` and used its parent directory, which assumes the git dir sits inside its own worktree — false whenever `.git` is a file or `--separate-git-dir` is in play. `ledgerRoot()` was dropped in the rebase; main's implementation is what ships. The investigation below stands as the record of how the defect was found and confirmed, not as a description of code in this commit. Risk-checked first: `run-ci.mjs` is the only writer and nothing reads the ledger programmatically (`docs/hook-enforcement.md:74` states this outright), so relocating the write cannot break a consumer. CLAUDE.md §8 already specified this behaviour — the code simply never implemented it, so no governance-doc edit is needed. The orphan record in this worktree was deleted; the primary checkout's legitimate `main` PASS record for the same sha was confirmed intact afterward.

   (c) **One `run-ci.mjs` fix is unique to this branch and does ship: `CHROMIUM_BLOCKED_PORTS`.** `derivePort()` draws from 6200–6899, which contains Chromium's hard-blocked ports 6665–6669 and 6697. This worktree's path hashed onto 6697; Chromium refuses it as `ERR_UNSAFE_PORT` while `isPortFree()` asks only the OS, which reports it free. The result was `test:a11y` failing 949 of 952 specs on connection — an all-fail signature, not an accessibility finding.    Not changed, and verified rather than assumed this time: `.claude/memory/violations.md` line 549 records a stale claim I made earlier in this ticket. It is a dated entry in a genuine append-only history, and every live source of truth has since been corrected, so amending it would be rewriting the record rather than fixing anything.

DS-167's own merge (PR #6) was the eighth consecutive merge to hit the same `/pr-merge` Gate 5/Gate 7 ordering defect, and the first to hit a second, worse one. J's instruction was to stop re-reporting it at every merge and fix it here rather than opening a new ticket.

(b) **Gate 7 deletes the ticket worktree with no check for uncommitted work in it.** New — it first bit on DS-167, because this was the first merge where the ticket worktree held uncommitted content that was itself allowlisted (`session-log.md` additions that had not yet been carried into the main checkout).
