title: Workflow robustness: four gate/skill defects plus mechanical enforcement for version sync and ticket creation
notes:
Two defects found during the 2026-09-01 post-DS-167 session. Both are workflow infrastructure, neither is on the main-branch allowlist, so both need a feature branch and a PR. Filed together because they were found together and are individually too small to warrant separate tickets — they share nothing else.

## Defect 1 — `run-ci.mjs` strands clean-room worktrees that nothing can ever reclaim

### What happened

`/private/tmp/mms-ci-f413f86bf7eb-10274` was found registered in `git worktree list`, detached at `f413f86`, 448M on disk, created 2026-08-31 16:52. It was removed manually on 2026-09-01 with J's explicit authorization.

### Why it was there

Not the documented failure mode. `tearDownCleanRoom` (`run-ci.mjs:688`) already warns when `git worktree remove --force` unregisters a worktree but leaves the directory — this one was still **registered**, so that path is ruled out. And it was not deliberately kept: `test-results/ci-runs/f413f86*.json` records `"result": "pass"` with no failed steps, so neither arm of `keepWorktree = !IN_PLACE && (!passed || KEEP)` (`run-ci.mjs:773`) applied.

Teardown never ran at all. The process died between the ledger write and the teardown call.

### Why nothing reclaims it

`setUpCleanRoom` calls `git worktree prune` on every run (`run-ci.mjs:612`), which looks like a sweeper and is not. `prune` only drops registrations whose **directory is gone**. A leftover whose directory still exists is skipped — on that run and on every run after it, forever. So the leak is self-perpetuating: each stranded clean room is a permanent 400M+ that no future gate run will ever notice or reclaim.

### Why the existing signal handlers do not cover it

`run-ci.mjs:552-560` installs SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers, but they only signal `activeChild` and `process.exit(130)`. They never touch the clean room. So even the interruption case they were written for — Ctrl-C during a gate run — strands the worktree.

### Fix shape

Two parts, because one cannot cover the other:

1. **Teardown on interrupt.** The existing handlers should tear the clean room down before exiting, unless it is being deliberately kept. This covers Ctrl-C and ordinary termination — the common case.
2. **Reclaim sweep at startup.** SIGKILL, a crash, and a hard power loss cannot be trapped, so part 1 can never be complete. `setUpCleanRoom` needs to sweep abandoned `mms-ci-*` worktrees itself, since `prune` provably will not.

The sweep must not touch a *live* concurrent run's clean room — two worktrees can legitimately gate at once, which is why the path carries `-${process.pid}` in the first place. Use that: parse the pid out of the directory name and reclaim only when the process is gone. Add an age floor as a guard against pid reuse. Announce what is reclaimed rather than doing it silently.

## Defect 2 — `/update-docs` Step 3 omits `README.md`'s header version line

`README.md:3` carries `**Version:** X.Y.Z | **Status:** ...` — a live version claim, distinct from the `## Version History` section.

Step 1 reads that line (`head -5 README.md`) and never writes it. Step 3 describes only the Version History insertion. So the header line is not in the command's touchpoint list at all, and the file is not covered by Step 9's `git add` on account of that step — it rides along only because README is staged for the history edit.

It was caught during the v0.25.0 bump on 2026-09-01 by Step 8's grep-for-the-old-version backstop, which is the second time that backstop has caught a touchpoint the step list omits (DS-170's Installation pages were the first, and were fixed structurally by deriving from `pkg.version` — not available to README, which is static markdown).

Step 8 has one hole worth noting but not fixing here: it greps for the *immediately previous* version only, so a file stranded on an older version stays stranded. A scan on 2026-09-01 found none, so this is theoretical today.

### Fix shape

Add `README.md:3`'s header line to Step 3 explicitly, in both `.claude/commands/update-docs.md` and its Copilot mirror `.github/prompts/update-docs.prompt.md`.

## Why this was filed at all

Both defects were reported to J as open items awaiting a decision rather than fixed on discovery. That inverted the standing rule — fix workflow defects at first discovery, in the skill file and its mirror; do not park them as J's call. Recorded here because the parking, not the defects, was the actual failure.

## Two further defects, found by verifying the fix

Writing the verification exposed two more, both of which would have shipped silently inside the fix for Defect 1.

### Defect 3 — the reclaim sweep's prefix match could never fire on macOS

`tmpdir()` returns `/tmp`, but `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp` and git reports every worktree through its resolved realpath. So `git worktree list` emits `/private/tmp/mms-ci-…` while the sweep's prefix was `/tmp/mms-ci-` — `startsWith` matches nothing, on the one platform this runs on. The sweep would have been an expensive no-op that looked correct in review. Caught only because planting a decoy worktree showed git listing it under `/private/tmp`. Fixed by matching against both the resolved and unresolved prefixes.

### Defect 4 — the interrupt handlers never actually ran their teardown

Pre-existing, and inherited by the first draft of the fix. The handlers deferred the SIGKILL escalation and `process.exit(130)` into `setTimeout(…, 2000).unref()`. The gate body is a straight-line synchronous script, so once the child dies it runs on to completion and exits before an unref'd timer can ever come due.

Verified live: a SIGINT mid-`build-storybook` produced an ordinary `❌ FAIL — aborted at build-storybook`, a ledger record, exit code 1, and no interrupt notice at all. The abort was indistinguishable from a genuine gate failure, and the worktree was kept on the `!passed` arm of `keepWorktree` rather than torn down. Adding teardown inside that timer would have changed nothing.

Fixed by making the whole handler synchronous — `Atomics.wait` for the grace period — so it completes before the gate body can resume.

One side effect worth recording: that aborted verification run overwrote the untracked `pass` ledger record for `3dd0621` with a `fail`. It was restored by re-running the full gate cleanly against the same SHA (17/17 PASS, 2m 26s). With Defect 4 fixed an interrupt exits before the ledger write, so it can no longer record a phantom failure.

## Verification

1. **Reclaim sweep** — planted a registered worktree at `/private/tmp/mms-ci-deadbeef1234-31000` owned by a dead pid, mtime backdated two hours; the next gate run reported `reclaimed 1 abandoned clean-room worktree(s)` and it was gone from `git worktree list`.
2. **Interrupt teardown** — SIGINT to the owning pid mid-`typecheck` printed `interrupted — removing the clean-room worktree`, exited, and left the room absent from both `git worktree list` and disk, with the ledger record byte-identical (no phantom record).
3. **Full gate** — 17/17 steps PASS against `3dd0621`, clean room torn down normally on the success path.

## Scope extension — converting the prose-only rules into mechanical ones

J asked, after the four defects above were fixed, whether these workflow flaggings would recur. The honest answer was no, not with confidence: Defect 1's fix is mechanical and will hold, but Defect 2's fix was a *sentence added to a command file*, and ticket creation — the rule broken to file this very ticket — had no enforcement at all. CLAUDE.md §5.4 already names that class: prose is soft, AI-dependent enforcement. Every prior recurrence of unapproved ticket creation (five of them) had been answered with another memory entry and a sharper rule, i.e. with more prose.

J approved closing both gaps under this ticket.

### Gap A — version touchpoints, asserted rather than described

`scripts/check-version-sync.mjs` takes `package.json` as the single source of truth and asserts all six touchpoints against it: README's header line, README's `(Current …)` Version History entry, `WhatsNew.stories.ts`'s current entry, `Welcome.stories.ts`'s version line, and both `package-lock.json` version fields. It also refuses more than one entry marked `(Current …)`.

The two Developer Guide Installation pages are deliberately absent — DS-170 made them derive from `pkg.version`, so they cannot drift, and re-hardcoding them would put `/update-docs` back to needing a PR to finish its own job on `main`.

A **vanished anchor is a failure, not a pass.** A probe that silently matches nothing is indistinguishable from a passing check, which is the exact way the prose list went stale twice.

It runs in two places on purpose:
- `.husky/pre-commit` check 7, when any touchpoint is staged. This is the one that matters — `/update-docs` commits *before* it gates, and post-commit is code lock, so a gate-only catch forces STOP-and-ask-J rather than a fix. Like check 6 it reads the working tree, not the index.
- `npm run ci` as `validate:version-sync`, against the committed SHA in the clean room. Definitive, and the only coverage for a path that reaches `main` without `/update-docs` at all.

Also rewrote `/update-docs` Step 8 on both tracks into 8a (blocking, mechanical) and 8b (the discovery grep), and recorded 8b's own limit inline: it searches for the *immediately previous* version, so a file stranded on an older version stays invisible to it. 8a asserts forward and has no such hole.

Registered in `verify-gates.mjs`. Its mutation inserts a bogus `0.0.0-gate-negative-test` ahead of the real version rather than hardcoding a version number — a case pinned to `0.25.0` would become a silent no-op at the next bump, which is the same staleness class the gate exists to catch.

### Gap B — ticket creation, rule 16

Two hooks, because a rule enforced on one surface is not enforced:
- `tracker-status-guard.sh` now runs a creation check **first and unconditionally**, before any status logic. That ordering is the point: the pre-DS-172 hook only examined transitions *into* `committed`/`done`, so a brand-new file written straight at `backlog` made no transition and sailed past every check it had.
- `violation-guard.sh` check 4 covers the Bash surface — `cp`/`mv`/`tee`/`touch`/`install` and `>`/`>>` redirects into `tracker/tasks/DS-NNN.json`. Without it the Write tool is gated while a one-line shell redirect walks straight past.

Both gate on `/tmp/ticket-create-approved`, consumed on use — one flag, one ticket. A surviving flag would silently authorize the next unrelated creation, which is this rule's failure mode wearing a different hat.

The Bash pattern's false-positive surface was checked rather than assumed: every occurrence of `tracker/tasks/` across `.claude/skills`, `.claude/commands`, `.github/prompts` and `scripts/` is a read or git plumbing (`git add`, `git ls-tree`, `jq`, `node tracker/build.cjs`). No sanctioned flow writes a ticket file from bash at all.

`/tracker-add` is the one sanctioned creation path and self-touches the flag as its own preceding call, the same documented-exception shape as `/publish-npm` Gate 5b — **and only when J's own message supplied the `title`**, which is what makes the invocation itself the approval. An inferred title is not an approval. Its Copilot mirror was also badly stale, still describing the pre-DS-141 single-array `tracker/tasks.json` model that is now a generated build artifact; rewritten to match.

Rule 16 added to `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — rule count 15 → 16, the flag list, rule 9's description, and a note under the status-enforcement table explaining that the table governs an existing ticket's status while creation is a separate gate.

### Gap B verification

Added nine cases to `scripts/test-governance-hooks.sh` (already a `npm run ci` step, so they gate every commit from here on): creation blocked without the flag; blocked at `backlog` and `in-progress` alike, not just `committed`/`done`; the flag allows exactly one creation and is consumed; editing an existing ticket needs no flag; rule 3's `done`-without-a-commit block survives the insertion; six shell write forms blocked; twelve real read/plumbing commands not blocked; the Bash flag consumed after one use; and checks 1-3 (force-push, `rm -r`, the grep carve-out, dxhub writes) still firing after check 4 was added.

The harness rewrites each hook's flag path to a scratch file during the fixture copy — the same technique already used for the commit-guard stub. The real `/tmp/ticket-create-approved` is never created, read, or deleted by the suite; a flag left behind by a test would silently authorize the next real ticket creation. Confirmed absent after the run.

### Scope-extension results

- `npm run test:governance-hooks` — 31 passed, 0 failed (was 22).
- `node scripts/check-governance-docs.mjs` — passed.
- `npm run verify-gates` — 11 LIVE, 0 INERT, 0 DISCONNECTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE, 5 SKIPPED, PASS. `check-version-sync` reports LIVE.
- `check-version-sync.mjs` proved against all three of its failure modes live (drifted header line, two `(Current …)` entries, vanished anchor), each perturbation reverted and the tree confirmed clean.

### What is still prose

Stated plainly rather than left implied. Rule 16's hooks are Claude Code PreToolUse hooks; **in Copilot they do not fire** (§5.4). The rule is identical on both tracks, the backstop is not. And no hook can read the conversation, so "did J name this ticket?" remains a judgment call at the moment the flag is touched — what changed is that the judgment now has to be made deliberately, at a gate, instead of never being made at all.

Merged in PR #8.
